verses.1:1: These are the names of the sons of Israel who went into Egypt together with Jacob their father; each one entered with his whole household:
verses.1:4: Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.
verses.1:5: Now Joseph was in Egypt; and all the souls from Jacob were seventy-five.
verses.1:6: And Joseph died, and all his brothers, and all that generation.
verses.1:7: But the sons of Israel increased and multiplied and teemed and grew very, very strong; and the land multiplied them.
verses.1:8: Then another king arose over Egypt, who did not know Joseph.
verses.1:9: And he said to his nation, "Look, the race of the sons of Israel is a great multitude, and is stronger than we are.
verses.1:10: Come, therefore, let us outwit them, so that it does not multiply, and whenever war happens to us, these also will be joined to the adversaries, and having waged war against us, they will depart from the land."
verses.1:11: So he set overseers of the works over them, so that they might afflict them in the works; and they built fortified cities for Pharaoh: Pithom, and Rameses, and On, which is Heliopolis.
verses.1:12: Yet the more they humbled them, so much the more numerous they became, and they grew very, very strong; and the Egyptians recoiled in disgust from the sons of Israel.
verses.1:13: And the Egyptians oppressed the sons of Israel by force,
verses.1:14: and made their life painful with harsh works, in clay and brickmaking and in all the works in the fields, according to all the works with which they enslaved them with force.
verses.1:15: And the king of the Egyptians spoke to the midwives of the Hebrews, to the one of them whose name was Shiphrah, and the name of the second was Puah;
verses.1:16: and he said, "When you act as midwives for the Hebrew women and they are about to give birth, if it is a male, kill it; but if it is a female, preserve it alive."
verses.1:17: But the midwives feared God, and did not do as the king of Egypt commanded them, and they kept the males alive.
verses.1:18: So the king of Egypt summoned the midwives and said to them, "Why is it that you have done this thing and kept the males alive?"
verses.1:19: And the midwives said to Pharaoh, "The Hebrew women are not like the women of Egypt, for they give birth before the midwives come in to them, and they gave birth."
verses.1:20: And God dealt well with the midwives, and the people multiplied and grew very strong.
verses.1:21: Because the midwives feared God, they made houses for themselves.
verses.1:22: Then Pharaoh commanded all his people, saying, "Every male that is born to the Hebrews, throw into the river; and every female, keep it alive."
verses.2:1: Now there was a certain man from the tribe of Levi who took one of the daughters of Levi.
verses.2:2: And she conceived and bore a male; and seeing that he was handsome, they sheltered him for three months.
verses.2:3: But when they could no longer hide him, his mother took a basket for him and coated it with bitumen-pitch, and placed the child in it, and set it in the marsh beside the river.
verses.2:4: And his sister kept watch from a distance to learn what would happen to him.
verses.2:5: Now the daughter of Pharaoh went down to bathe at the river, and her female attendants were walking beside the river; and seeing the basket in the marsh, she sent her attendant and took it up.
verses.2:6: And opening it, she saw a child crying in the basket; and the daughter of Pharaoh spared him and said, "This is one of the children of the Hebrews."
verses.2:7: Then his sister said to the daughter of Pharaoh, "Do you want me to call for you a nursing woman from the Hebrews, and she will nurse the child for you?"
verses.2:8: And the daughter of Pharaoh said, "Go." So the young woman went and called the mother of the child.
verses.2:9: And the daughter of Pharaoh said to her, "Keep this child safe for me and nurse him for me, and I will give you the wages." So the woman took the child and nursed him.
verses.2:10: When the child had grown up, she brought him in to the daughter of Pharaoh, and he became a son to her; and she named his name Moses, saying, "Out of the water I took him up."
verses.2:11: Now it happened in those many days that when Moses had grown up, he went out to his brothers, the sons of Israel. And observing their toil, he saw an Egyptian man beating a certain Hebrew of his own brothers, the sons of Israel.
verses.2:12: And looking around this way and that, he saw no one; and striking down the Egyptian, he hid him in the sand.
verses.2:13: And going out on the second day, he saw two Hebrew men fighting with one another, and he said to the one doing wrong, "Why are you beating your neighbor?"
verses.2:14: And he said, "Who appointed you ruler and judge over us? Do you intend to kill me in the way you killed the Egyptian yesterday?" Then Moses became afraid and said, "Has this matter become known like this?"
verses.2:15: Now Pharaoh heard of this matter, and he sought to kill Moses; so Moses withdrew from the presence of Pharaoh and settled in the land of Midian; and having come into the land of Midian, he sat down by the well.
verses.2:16: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters, who were shepherding the sheep of their father Jethro; and coming there, they drew water until they filled the troughs, to water the sheep of their father Jethro.
verses.2:17: But the shepherds came and were driving them away; and Moses stood up and rescued them, and drew water for them and watered their sheep.
verses.2:18: Then they came to Reuel their father; and he said to them, "Why have you been so quick to come today?"
verses.2:19: And they said, "An Egyptian man rescued us from the shepherds, and he drew water for us and watered our sheep."
verses.2:20: And he said to his daughters, "And where is he? And why have you left the man behind? Call him, therefore, so that he may eat bread."
verses.2:21: So Moses took up residence with the man; and he gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses as a wife.
verses.2:22: And the woman conceived and bore a son; and Moses named his name Gershom, saying, "Because I am a sojourner in a foreign land."
verses.2:23: Now after those many days, the king of Egypt died; and the sons of Israel groaned because of the works and cried out, and their outcry went up to God from the works.
verses.2:24: And God heard their groaning, and God remembered His covenant with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob.
verses.2:25: And God looked upon the sons of Israel, and He was made known to them.
verses.3:1: Now Moses was shepherding the sheep of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian; and he led the sheep beyond the wilderness and came to Mount Horeb.
verses.3:2: And an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a fire of flame out of the bush; and he saw that the bush was burning with fire, yet the bush was not being burned up.
verses.3:3: And Moses said, "I will turn aside and see this great sight, why the bush is not burned up."
verses.3:4: And when the Lord saw that he was drawing near to look, the Lord called him out of the bush, saying, "Moses, Moses." And he said, "What is it?"
verses.3:5: And He said, "Do not draw near here; untie the sandal from your feet, for the place on which you are standing is holy ground."
verses.3:6: And He said, "I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob." And Moses turned away his face, for he was afraid to gaze before God.
verses.3:7: And the Lord said to Moses, "I have surely seen the affliction of My people who are in Egypt, and I have heard their cry because of the taskmasters; for I know their anguish,
verses.3:8: and I have come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians and to bring them out of that land, and to bring them into a good and vast land, into a land flowing with milk and honey, into the place of the Canaanites and Hittites and Amorites and Perizzites and Girgashites and Hivites and Jebusites.
verses.3:9: And now, look, the cry of the sons of Israel has come to Me, and I have seen the oppression with which the Egyptians are oppressing them.
verses.3:10: And now, come, let Me send you to Pharaoh king of Egypt, and you shall bring My people, the sons of Israel, out of the land of Egypt."
verses.3:11: And Moses said to God, "Who am I that I should go to Pharaoh king of Egypt, and that I should bring the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt?"
verses.3:12: And God spoke to Moses, saying, "I will be with you; and this will be the sign for you that I will send you out: when you bring My people out of Egypt, you will also worship God on this mountain."
verses.3:13: And Moses said to God, "Look, I will go out to the sons of Israel and say to them, 'The God of our fathers has sent me to you.' They will ask me, 'What is His name?' What shall I say to them?"
verses.3:14: And God spoke to Moses, saying, "I am the One who is." And He said, "Thus you shall say to the sons of Israel: 'The One who is has sent me to you.'"
verses.3:15: And God said again to Moses, "Thus you shall say to the sons of Israel: 'The Lord, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you.' This is My eternal name, and a memorial to generations of generations.
verses.3:16: Go, therefore, gather the council of elders of the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them, 'The Lord, the God of your fathers, has appeared to me, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, saying, "I have surely watched over you and all that has happened to you in Egypt,"
verses.3:17: and He said, "I will bring you up out of the affliction of the Egyptians into the land of the Canaanites and Hittites and Amorites and Perizzites and Girgashites and Hivites and Jebusites, into a land flowing with milk and honey."'
verses.3:18: And they will listen to your voice; and you and the council of elders of Israel shall go in to Pharaoh king of Egypt, and you shall say to him, 'The God of the Hebrews has summoned us; let us go, therefore, a three days' journey into the wilderness, so that we may sacrifice to our God.'
verses.3:19: But I know that Pharaoh king of Egypt will not let you go, except by a mighty hand;
verses.3:20: and stretching out My hand, I will strike the Egyptians with all My wonders which I will do among them, and after these things he will send you out.
verses.3:21: And I will give favor to this people before the Egyptians; and when you depart, you will not go away empty-handed;
verses.3:22: a woman shall ask from her neighbor and housemate for articles of silver and gold and clothing, and you shall put them on your sons and on your daughters; and plunder the Egyptians."
verses.4:1: Then Moses answered and said, "If they do not believe me and do not listen to my voice—for they will say, 'God has not appeared to you'—what shall I say to them?"
verses.4:2: And the Lord said to him, "What is this that is in your hand?" And he said, "A staff."
verses.4:3: And He said, "Throw it onto the ground." And he threw it onto the ground, and it became a serpent; and Moses fled from it.
verses.4:4: And the Lord said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand and take hold of the tail." So he stretched out his hand and took hold of the tail, and it became a staff in his hand—
verses.4:5: "so that they may believe you that the God of their fathers has appeared to you, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob."
verses.4:6: And the Lord said to him again, "Put your hand into your bosom." And he put his hand into his bosom; and he brought his hand out of his bosom, and his hand became like snow.
verses.4:7: And He said again, "Put your hand into your bosom." And he put his hand into his bosom; and he brought it out of his bosom, and it was restored again to the color of its flesh.
verses.4:8: "And if they do not believe you and do not listen to the voice of the first sign, they will believe you at the voice of the latter sign.
verses.4:9: And it will be that if they do not believe you through these two signs and do not listen to your voice, you shall take from the water of the river and pour it out onto the dry ground, and the water that you take from the river will be blood upon the dry ground."
verses.4:10: Then Moses said to the Lord, "Please, Lord, I am not competent—neither before yesterday, nor before the third day, nor since You began to speak to Your servant; I am weak-voiced and slow-tongued."
verses.4:11: And the Lord said to Moses, "Who gave a mouth to man, and who made the hard of hearing and the deaf, the seeing and the blind? Is it not I, God?
verses.4:12: And now go, and I will open your mouth, and I will instruct you in what you are to speak."
verses.4:13: And Moses said, "Please, Lord, appoint another capable person whom You will send."
verses.4:14: And the Lord, becoming enraged with anger against Moses, said, "Look, is there not Aaron your brother, the Levite? I know that he will surely speak for you; and look, he himself will come out to meet you, and when he sees you, he will rejoice in himself.
verses.4:15: And you shall speak to him and put My words into his mouth; and I will open your mouth and his mouth, and I will instruct you in what you shall do.
verses.4:16: And he himself will speak for you to the people, and he will be your mouth, while you will be for him in the matters pertaining to God.
verses.4:17: And this staff that was turned into a serpent you shall take in your hand, with which you shall perform the signs."
verses.4:18: Then Moses went and returned to Jethro his father-in-law and said, "I will go and return to my brothers who are in Egypt, and I will see if they are still alive." And Jethro said to Moses, "Go in good health." And after those many days, the king of Egypt died.
verses.4:19: And the Lord said to Moses in Midian, "Go, depart to Egypt; for all those seeking your life have died."
verses.4:20: So Moses took his wife and children, mounted them on the beasts of burden, and returned to Egypt; and Moses took the staff from God in his hand.
verses.4:21: And the Lord said to Moses, "As you go and return to Egypt, see all the wonders that I have put in your hands—you shall perform them before Pharaoh; but I will harden his heart, and he will by no means send the people away.
verses.4:22: And you shall say to Pharaoh, 'Thus says the Lord: Israel is My firstborn son,
verses.4:23: and I said to you: Send My people away so that they may serve Me; now if you are not willing to send them away, see then, I am going to kill your firstborn son.'"
verses.4:24: And it happened on the way, at the lodging place, that an angel of the Lord met him and sought to kill him.
verses.4:25: And Zipporah took a stone and circumcised the foreskin of her son, and she fell down at the feet and said, "The blood of the circumcision of my child has stopped."
verses.4:26: And he departed from him, because she said, "The blood of the circumcision of my child has stopped."
verses.4:27: And the Lord said to Aaron, "Go into the wilderness to meet Moses." And he went and met him at the mountain of God, and they kissed one another.
verses.4:28: And Moses reported to Aaron all the words of the Lord that He had sent, and all the sayings that He had commanded him.
verses.4:29: Then Moses and Aaron went and gathered the council of elders of the sons of Israel.
verses.4:30: And Aaron spoke all these words that God had spoken to Moses, and he performed the signs before the people.
verses.4:31: And the people believed and rejoiced that God had visited the sons of Israel and that He had seen their affliction; and bowing down, the people worshiped.
verses.5:1: And after these things, Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh and said to him, "Thus says the Lord God of Israel: 'Send My people away, so that they may celebrate a festival to Me in the wilderness.'"
verses.5:2: And Pharaoh said, "Who is He, that I should listen to His voice so as to send the sons of Israel away? I do not know the Lord, and I will not send Israel away."
verses.5:3: And they said to him, "The God of the Hebrews has summoned us; therefore we will go a journey of three days into the wilderness, so that we may sacrifice to our God, so that death or slaughter may not meet us."
verses.5:4: And the king of Egypt said to them, "Why, Moses and Aaron, are you turning my people aside from the labors? Depart, each one of you to his labors."
verses.5:5: And Pharaoh said, "Look, now the people are very numerous; therefore let us not give them rest from the labors."
verses.5:6: So Pharaoh commanded the taskmasters of the people and the scribes, saying,
verses.5:7: "No longer shall straw continue to be given to the people for brickmaking, as yesterday and the third day; let them go themselves and gather straw for themselves.
verses.5:8: And the quota of brickmaking that they make each day you shall impose on them; you shall not reduce it at all; for they are idle, and therefore they have been crying out, saying, 'Let us arise and sacrifice to our God.'
verses.5:9: Let the labors of these men be made heavy, and let them be occupied with these things, and let them not be occupied with empty words."
verses.5:10: And the taskmasters and the scribes pressed them hard and spoke to the people, saying, "Thus says Pharaoh: 'I am no longer giving you straw;
verses.5:11: go yourselves and gather straw for yourselves wherever you may find it, for nothing at all is being reduced from your quota.'"
verses.5:12: And the people were scattered throughout all the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.
verses.5:13: And the taskmasters pressed them hard, saying, "Complete the labors required each day, just as when the straw was given to you."
verses.5:14: And the scribes of the race of the sons of Israel, who had been appointed over them by Pharaoh's overseers, were flogged and were asked, "Why have you not completed your quotas of brickmaking, as yesterday and the third day, and that of today?"
verses.5:15: Then the scribes of the sons of Israel went in and cried out to Pharaoh, saying, "Why are you dealing this way with your household servants?
verses.5:16: Straw is not given to your household servants, yet they tell us to make brick; and look, your servants have been flogged. Therefore you will wrong your people."
verses.5:17: And he said to them, "You are idle, you are idlers; therefore you say, 'Let us go, let us sacrifice to our God.'
verses.5:18: Now therefore go and work; for the straw will not be given to you, yet you shall deliver the quota of brickmaking."
verses.5:19: And the scribes of the sons of Israel saw themselves in trouble, as it was said, "You shall not fall short of the daily requirement of brickmaking."
verses.5:20: And they met Moses and Aaron coming to meet them, as they were going out from Pharaoh,
verses.5:21: and they said to them, "May God look upon you and judge, because you have made our odor loathsome before Pharaoh and before his servants, putting a sword into his hands to kill us."
verses.5:22: Then Moses returned to the Lord and said, "Please, Lord, why have You harmed this people? And why have You sent me?
verses.5:23: And since I went to Pharaoh to speak in Your name, he has harmed this people, and You have not rescued Your people."
verses.6:1: And the Lord said to Moses, "Now you will see what I will do to Pharaoh; for with a mighty hand he will send them out, and with an uplifted arm he will drive them out of his land."
verses.6:2: Now God spoke to Moses and said to him, "I am the Lord.
verses.6:3: And I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, being their God, and I did not make My name, the Lord, known to them.
verses.6:4: And I established My covenant with them so as to give them the land of the Canaanites, the land in which they have sojourned, on which they also sojourned.
verses.6:5: And I heard the groaning of the sons of Israel, whom the Egyptians are enslaving, and I remembered your covenant.
verses.6:6: Go, speak to the sons of Israel, saying, 'I am the Lord, and I will bring you out from the domination of the Egyptians, and I will rescue you from slavery, and I will redeem you with an uplifted arm and great judgment.
verses.6:7: And I will take you to Myself as a people for Me, and I will be your God, and you will know that I am the Lord your God, who brought you out from the oppression of the Egyptians.
verses.6:8: And I will bring you out into the land toward which I stretched out My hand to give it to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and I will give it to you as an inheritance. I am the Lord.'"
verses.6:9: And Moses spoke in this way to the sons of Israel, but they did not listen to Moses because of faintheartedness and because of the harsh labors.
verses.6:10: Then the Lord said to Moses, saying,
verses.6:11: "Go in, speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt, so that he may send out the sons of Israel from his land."
verses.6:12: But Moses spoke before the Lord, saying, "Look, the sons of Israel did not listen to me, and how will Pharaoh listen to me? And I am inarticulate."
verses.6:13: And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, and He gave them a charge to Pharaoh king of Egypt, so as to send out the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt.
verses.6:14: And these are the leaders of the houses of their clans. The sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel: Hanoch and Pallu, Hezron and Carmi; this is the kindred of Reuben.
verses.6:15: And the sons of Simeon: Jemuel and Jamin and Ohad and Jachin and Zohar and Shaul, the one from the Phoenician woman; these are the clans of the sons of Simeon.
verses.6:16: And these are the names of the sons of Levi according to their kindreds: Gershon and Kohath and Merari; and the years of the life of Levi were one hundred thirty-seven.
verses.6:17: And these are the sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei, houses of their clan.
verses.6:18: And the sons of Kohath: Amram and Issachar, Hebron and Uzziel; and the years of the life of Kohath were one hundred thirty years.
verses.6:19: And the sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These are the houses of the clans of Levi according to their kindred.
verses.6:20: And Amram took Jochebed, the daughter of his father's brother, for himself as a wife, and she bore to him both Aaron and Moses, and Miriam their sister; and the years of the life of Amram were one hundred thirty-two years.
verses.6:21: And the sons of Izhar: Korah and Nepheg and Zichri.
verses.6:22: And the sons of Uzziel: Elizaphan and Segri.
verses.6:23: And Aaron took Elisheba, the daughter of Amminadab, the sister of Nahshon, for himself as a wife, and she bore to him Nadab and Abihu and Eleazar and Ithamar.
verses.6:24: And the sons of Korah: Assir and Elkanah and Abiasar; these are the generations of Korah.
verses.6:25: And Eleazar, the son of Aaron, took one of the daughters of Putiel for himself as a wife, and she bore Phinehas to him. These are the heads of the clan of the Levites according to their generations.
verses.6:26: This is Aaron and Moses, to whom God spoke, to bring out the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt with their force.
verses.6:27: These are the ones who spoke with Pharaoh king of Egypt; and they brought out the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt, this same Aaron and Moses.
verses.6:28: On the day when the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
verses.6:29: the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, "I am the Lord. Speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt, and I am speaking to you."
verses.6:30: And Moses said before the Lord, "Look, I am weak-voiced, and how will Pharaoh listen to me?"
verses.7:1: And the Lord said to Moses, saying, "Look, I have given you as a god to Pharaoh, and Aaron your brother will be your prophet.
verses.7:2: And you will speak to him all the things that I command you, and Aaron your brother will speak to Pharaoh so that he may send out the sons of Israel from his land.
verses.7:3: But I will harden the heart of Pharaoh, and I will multiply My signs and wonders in the land of Egypt.
verses.7:4: And Pharaoh will not listen to you; and I will lay My hand upon Egypt, and with My power I will bring out My people, the sons of Israel, from the land of Egypt with great vengeance.
verses.7:5: And all the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord, as I stretch out My hand upon Egypt; and I will bring out the sons of Israel from their midst."
verses.7:6: And Moses and Aaron did just as the Lord commanded them; so they did.
verses.7:7: Now Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron his brother was eighty-three years old, when he spoke to Pharaoh.
verses.7:8: And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, saying,
verses.7:9: "And if Pharaoh speaks to you, saying, 'Give us a sign or a wonder,' then you will say to Aaron your brother, 'Take the staff and throw it upon the ground before Pharaoh and before his attendants,' and it will become a dragon."
verses.7:10: So Moses and Aaron went in before Pharaoh and his attendants, and they did so, just as the Lord commanded them; and Aaron threw the staff before Pharaoh and before his attendants, and it became a dragon.
verses.7:11: Then Pharaoh called together the wise men of Egypt and the sorcerers; and the enchanters of the Egyptians also did the same by their sorceries,
verses.7:12: and each one threw his staff, and they became dragons; and Aaron's staff swallowed up their staffs.
verses.7:13: And the heart of Pharaoh grew strong, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had commanded them.
verses.7:14: Then the Lord said to Moses, "The heart of Pharaoh is weighed down so as not to send out the people.
verses.7:15: Go to Pharaoh in the morning; look, he is going out to the water, and you will be meeting him at the bank of the river; and you will take in your hand the staff that was turned into a snake,
verses.7:16: and you will say to him, 'The Lord, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to you, saying, "Send out My people so that they may serve Me in the wilderness"; and look, you have not listened until now.
verses.7:17: Thus says the Lord: "By this you will know that I am the Lord: look, I am striking the water that is in the river with the staff that is in My hand, and it will turn into blood;
verses.7:18: and the fish that are in the river will die, and the river will stink, and the Egyptians will not be able to drink water from the river."'"
verses.7:19: And the Lord said to Moses, "Say to Aaron your brother, 'Take your staff in your hand, and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt, and over their rivers, and over their canals, and over their marshes, and over all their standing water, and it will become blood.'" And blood came to be in all the land of Egypt, both in the wood and in the stone.
verses.7:20: And Moses and Aaron did so, just as the Lord commanded them; and lifting up his staff, he struck the water that was in the river before Pharaoh and before his attendants, and all the water that was in the river turned into blood.
verses.7:21: And the fish that were in the river died, and the river stank, and the Egyptians were not able to drink water from the river, and the blood was in all the land of Egypt.
verses.7:22: And the enchanters of the Egyptians also did the same by their sorceries; and the heart of Pharaoh hardened, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had said.
verses.7:23: And Pharaoh turned around and went into his house, and he did not set his mind even on this.
verses.7:24: And all the Egyptians dug around the river so as to drink water from the river, and they were not able to drink water from the river.
verses.7:25: And seven days were fulfilled after the Lord struck the river.
verses.7:26: Then the Lord said to Moses, "Go in to Pharaoh, and you will say to him, 'Thus says the Lord: "Send out My people so that they may serve Me.
verses.7:27: And if you are not willing to send them out, look, I am striking all your borders with frogs.
verses.7:28: And the river will pour forth frogs; and coming up, they will enter into your houses, and into the inner chambers of your bedrooms, and upon your beds, and into the houses of your attendants and of your people, and in your dough and in your ovens;
verses.7:29: and upon you and upon your attendants and upon your people the frogs will come up."'"
verses.8:1: And the Lord said to Moses, "Say to Aaron your brother, 'Stretch out your staff with your hand over the rivers and over the canals and over the marshes, and bring up the frogs.'"
verses.8:2: And Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and he brought up the frogs; and the frogs were brought up and covered the land of Egypt.
verses.8:3: And the enchanters of the Egyptians also did likewise with their sorceries, and they brought up the frogs upon the land of Egypt.
verses.8:4: And Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, "Pray for me to the Lord, and let Him remove the frogs from me and from my people, and I will send them away, and let them sacrifice to the Lord."
verses.8:5: And Moses said to Pharaoh, "Appoint for me when I should pray for you and for your servants and for your people, to wipe out the frogs from you and from your people and from your houses; only in the river will they be left."
verses.8:6: And he said, "For tomorrow." So he said, "As you have spoken, so that you may see that there is no other besides the Lord;
verses.8:7: and the frogs will be removed from you and from your houses and from the courtyards and from your servants and from your people; only in the river will they be left."
verses.8:8: And Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh; and Moses cried out to the Lord concerning the appointed time of the frogs, as Pharaoh had appointed.
verses.8:9: And the Lord did just as Moses said, and the frogs died out of the houses and out of the courtyards and out of the fields;
verses.8:10: and they gathered them in heaps upon heaps, and the land stank.
verses.8:11: But when Pharaoh saw that relief had come, his heart became heavy, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had spoken.
verses.8:12: And the Lord said to Moses, "Say to Aaron, 'Stretch out your staff with your hand and strike the dust of the ground, and there will be gnats both on the people and on the four-footed animals and in all the land of Egypt.'"
verses.8:13: So Aaron stretched out his staff with his hand and struck the dust of the ground, and the gnats came to be on the people and on the four-footed animals; and in all the dust of the ground the gnats came to be.
verses.8:14: And the enchanters also did likewise with their sorceries to bring forth the gnats, and they were not able; and the gnats were on the people and on the four-footed animals.
verses.8:15: So the enchanters said to Pharaoh, "This is the finger of God." Yet Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had spoken.
verses.8:16: And the Lord said to Moses, "Rise early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh; and look, he will go out to the water, and you shall say to him, 'Thus says the Lord: Send away My people so that they may serve Me in the wilderness;
verses.8:17: but if you are not willing to send away My people, look, I am sending upon you and upon your servants and upon your people and upon your houses dog-flies, and the houses of the Egyptians will be filled with the dog-flies, and also the ground on which they are.
verses.8:18: And on that day I will wondrously set apart the land of Goshen, on which My people are, where the dog-flies will not be, so that you may know that I am the Lord, the Lord of all the earth.
verses.8:19: And I will make a distinction between My people and your people; and tomorrow this will happen upon the land.'"
verses.8:20: And the Lord did so, and the dog-flies came in a multitude into the houses of Pharaoh and into the houses of his servants and into all the land of Egypt; and the land was ruined by the dog-flies.
verses.8:21: And Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron, saying, "Go, sacrifice to your God in the land."
verses.8:22: And Moses said, "It is not possible for this matter to happen this way, for we will sacrifice the abominations of the Egyptians to the Lord our God; for if we sacrifice the abominations of the Egyptians before them, we will be stoned.
verses.8:23: We will go a three days' journey into the wilderness, and we will sacrifice to our God just as the Lord told us."
verses.8:24: And Pharaoh said, "I am sending you, and sacrifice to your God in the wilderness; only you shall not extend your journey far. Pray therefore for me to the Lord."
verses.8:25: And Moses said, "Look, I will go out from you and pray to God, and the dog-flies will depart from you and from your servants and your people tomorrow; do not continue any longer, Pharaoh, to deceive by not sending away the people to sacrifice to the Lord."
verses.8:26: And Moses went out from Pharaoh and prayed to God.
verses.8:27: And the Lord did just as Moses said, and He removed the dog-flies from Pharaoh and his servants and his people, and not even one was left.
verses.8:28: And Pharaoh made his heart heavy at this time as well, and he was not willing to send away the people.
verses.9:1: And the Lord said to Moses, "Go in to Pharaoh, and you shall say to him, 'Thus says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews: Send away My people so that they may serve Me;
verses.9:2: if then you are not willing to send away My people, but still hold onto them,
verses.9:3: look, the hand of the Lord will be upon your livestock that are in the fields, both on the horses and on the beasts of burden and the camels and cattle and sheep, a very great death.
verses.9:4: And at that time I will make a wondrous distinction between the livestock of the Egyptians and the livestock of the sons of Israel; not a single thing will die from all that belongs to the sons of Israel.'"
verses.9:5: And God set a time limit, saying, "Tomorrow the Lord will do this thing upon the land."
verses.9:6: And the Lord did this thing the next day, and all the livestock of the Egyptians died; but of the livestock of the sons of Israel not one died.
verses.9:7: And when Pharaoh saw that not one of all the livestock of the sons of Israel had died, Pharaoh's heart became heavy, and he did not send away the people.
verses.9:8: And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying, "Take your hands full of furnace soot, and let Moses scatter it toward the sky before Pharaoh and before his servants,
verses.9:9: and let it become fine dust over all the land of Egypt; and upon the people and upon the four-footed animals there will be sores, erupting blisters, both on the people and on the four-footed animals and in all the land of Egypt."
verses.9:10: And he took the soot of the furnace before Pharaoh, and Moses scattered it toward the sky; and there came to be sores, erupting blisters, on the people and on the four-footed animals.
verses.9:11: And the sorcerers could not stand before Moses because of the sores, for the sores were on the sorcerers and in all the land of Egypt.
verses.9:12: But the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had commanded.
verses.9:13: And the Lord said to Moses, "Rise early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh, and you shall say to him, 'Thus says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews: Send away My people so that they may serve Me.
verses.9:14: For at this present time I am sending out all My afflictions against your heart and that of your servants and of your people, so that you may know that there is no other like Me in all the earth.
verses.9:15: For now, stretching out My hand, I will strike you, and I will put your people to death, and you will be wiped out from the earth;
verses.9:16: and for this reason you were preserved, so that I may display My strength in you, and so that My name may be proclaimed in all the earth.
verses.9:17: Do you then still lay claim to My people, so as not to send them away?
verses.9:18: Look, at this hour tomorrow I am raining down very heavy hail, such as has not occurred in Egypt from the day it was founded until this day.
verses.9:19: Now therefore hurry to gather your livestock and all that you have in the field; for all the people and the livestock that belong to you in the field and do not enter a house, when the hail falls on them, they will die.'"
verses.9:20: The one among the servants of Pharaoh who feared the word of the Lord gathered his livestock into the houses;
verses.9:21: but whoever did not pay attention in his mind to the word of the Lord left the livestock in the fields.
verses.9:22: And the Lord said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand toward the sky, and there will be hail over all the land of Egypt, both on the people and the livestock and on every plant that is on the earth."
verses.9:23: And Moses stretched out his hand toward the sky, and the Lord gave thunders and hail, and fire ran along the earth; and the Lord rained hail upon all the land of Egypt.
verses.9:24: And there was the hail, and the fire flaming within the hail; and the hail was very heavy, such as had not occurred in Egypt from the day a nation came into being upon it.
verses.9:25: And the hail struck in all the land of Egypt, from human to livestock, and the hail struck every plant that was in the field, and the hail shattered all the trees that were in the fields;
verses.9:26: only in the land of Goshen, where the sons of Israel were, there was no hail.
verses.9:27: And Pharaoh sent and summoned Moses and Aaron and said to them, "I have sinned this time; the Lord is righteous, and I and my people are ungodly.
verses.9:28: Pray therefore for me to the Lord, and let there cease to be thunders of God and hail and fire; and I will send you away, and you will no longer continue to stay."
verses.9:29: And Moses said to him, "As soon as I go out of the city, I will spread out my hands, and the thunders will cease, and the hail and the rain will be no more, so that you may know that the earth belongs to the Lord.
verses.9:30: But as for you and your servants, I know that you do not yet fear God."
verses.9:31: Now the flax and the barley were struck, for the barley was standing ripe and the flax was producing seed;
verses.9:32: but the wheat and the spelt were not struck, for they were late.
verses.9:33: And Moses went out from Pharaoh outside the city and stretched out his hands to the Lord; and the thunders and the hail ceased, and the rain no longer dripped upon the earth.
verses.9:34: But when Pharaoh saw that the rain and the hail and the thunders had ceased, he continued to sin, and he made his own heart heavy, and that of his servants.
verses.9:35: And Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not send away the sons of Israel, just as the Lord had spoken to Moses.
verses.10:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, "Go in to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and that of his attendants, so that these signs may come upon them in succession,
verses.10:2: in order that you may recount in the ears of your children and to the children of your children all the ways I have mocked the Egyptians, and My signs that I performed among them; and you will know that I am the Lord."
verses.10:3: And Moses and Aaron went in before Pharaoh and said to him, "Thus says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews: 'How long are you unwilling to show reverence to Me? Send away My people so that they may serve Me.
verses.10:4: But if you are not willing to send away My people, look, at this hour tomorrow I am bringing abundant locusts upon all your borders;
verses.10:5: and they will cover the face of the land, and you will not be able to see the land; and they will devour all the remainder of the land that was left behind, which the hail left for you, and they will devour every tree growing for you upon the land;
verses.10:6: and your houses will be filled, and the houses of your attendants, and all the houses in all the land of the Egyptians—things that neither your fathers nor their great-grandfathers have ever seen, from the day they came to be upon the earth until this day.'" And Moses turned away and went out from Pharaoh.
verses.10:7: And the attendants of Pharaoh said to him, "How long will this be a snare to us? Send away the people so that they may serve their God. Or do you want to know that Egypt is destroyed?"
verses.10:8: And they brought both Moses and Aaron back to Pharaoh, and he said to them, "Go and serve your God. But who and who are the ones going?"
verses.10:9: And Moses said, "With our young men and elders we will go, with our sons and daughters and sheep and cattle, for it is a festival of the Lord."
verses.10:10: And he said to them, "So be it—the Lord be with you! Just as I am sending you away, shall I send your dependents too? See, evil lies before you.
verses.10:11: Not so! Instead, let the men go and serve God, for this is what you yourselves were seeking." And they drove them out from the presence of Pharaoh.
verses.10:12: And the Lord said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt, and let locusts come up upon the land, and they will devour every plant of the land and all the fruit of the trees that the hail left behind."
verses.10:13: And Moses lifted up the staff toward heaven and brought a south wind upon the land all that day and all the night; morning came, and the south wind took up the locusts,
verses.10:14: and brought them up over all the land of Egypt, and they settled upon all the borders of Egypt, exceedingly numerous; before them there have never been such locusts, and after these things it will not be so.
verses.10:15: And they covered the face of the land, and the land was ruined; and they devoured every plant of the land and all the fruit of the trees that was left from the hail; nothing green was left on the trees or in any plant of the field in the land of Egypt.
verses.10:16: And Pharaoh hurried to summon Moses and Aaron, saying, "I have sinned before the Lord your God and against you.
verses.10:17: Therefore forgive my sin just this once more, and pray to the Lord your God, and let Him remove this death from me."
verses.10:18: And Moses went out from Pharaoh and prayed to God.
verses.10:19: And the Lord shifted a strong wind from the sea, and it took up the locusts and cast them into the Red Sea; and not a single locust was left in all the land of Egypt.
verses.10:20: And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh, and he did not send away the sons of Israel.
verses.10:21: And the Lord said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand toward heaven, and let there be darkness over the land of Egypt, a palpable darkness."
verses.10:22: And Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and there came darkness, gloom, tempest over all the land of Egypt for three days;
verses.10:23: and no one saw his brother for three days, and no one rose up from his bed for three days; but for all the sons of Israel there was light in all the places where they lived.
verses.10:24: And Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron, saying, "Go, serve the Lord your God; only leave behind the sheep and the cattle, and let your dependents go away with you."
verses.10:25: And Moses said, "Rather, you yourself will also give us burnt offerings and sacrifices that we will offer to the Lord our God,
verses.10:26: and our livestock will go with us, and we will not leave behind a hoof; for from them we will take to serve the Lord our God, and we do not know with what we are to serve the Lord our God until we arrive there."
verses.10:27: And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh, and he was not willing to send them away.
verses.10:28: And Pharaoh said, "Go away from me! Watch yourself against seeing my face again, and on whatever day you appear before me, you will die."
verses.10:29: And Moses said, "You have spoken it; I will no longer appear before your face."
verses.11:1: And the Lord said to Moses, "Yet one more plague I will bring upon Pharaoh and upon Egypt, and after these things he will send you away from here; and when he sends you away, with everything he will surely drive you out.
verses.11:2: Speak secretly, therefore, in the ears of the people, and let each one ask his neighbor for articles of silver and gold and clothing."
verses.11:3: And the Lord gave favor to His people in the sight of the Egyptians, and they lent to them; and the man Moses became exceedingly great in the sight of the Egyptians and in the sight of Pharaoh and in the sight of all his attendants.
verses.11:4: And Moses said, "Thus says the Lord: 'Around midnight I am going into the midst of Egypt,
verses.11:5: and every firstborn in the land of Egypt will die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sits on the throne even to the firstborn of the maidservant who is beside the mill, and even to the firstborn of every animal;
verses.11:6: and there will be a great outcry throughout all the land of Egypt, such as has never occurred and such as will never occur again.
verses.11:7: And among all the sons of Israel not a dog will snarl with its tongue, not from man to animal, so that you may see how wondrously the Lord makes a distinction between the Egyptians and Israel.'
verses.11:8: And all these servants of yours will come down to me and bow down to me, saying, 'Go out, you and all your people whom you lead!' And after these things I will go out." And Moses went out from Pharaoh in anger.
verses.11:9: And the Lord said to Moses, "Pharaoh will not listen to you, so that I may greatly multiply My signs and wonders in the land of Egypt."
verses.11:10: Now Moses and Aaron performed all these signs and wonders in the land of Egypt before Pharaoh; and the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh, and he did not listen so as to send away the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt.
verses.12:1: Now the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,
verses.12:2: "This month is for you the beginning of months; it is the first for you among the months of the year.
verses.12:3: Speak to all the congregation of the sons of Israel, saying, 'On the tenth of this month let each of them take a sheep according to fathers' houses, each one a sheep according to a household.
verses.12:4: And if those in the house are too few to be sufficient for a sheep, he shall take along with himself his neighbor who is near to him; according to the number of souls, each shall reckon what is enough for himself for a sheep.
verses.12:5: It shall be for you a perfect sheep, a male a year old; you shall take it from the lambs and the young goats.
verses.12:6: And it shall be kept by you until the fourteenth of this month, and all the multitude of the congregation of the sons of Israel shall slaughter it toward evening.
verses.12:7: And they shall take some of the blood and put it on the two doorposts and on the lintel, on the houses in which they eat them.
verses.12:8: And they shall eat the flesh on this night, roasted with fire, and they shall eat unleavened bread with bitter herbs.
verses.12:9: You shall not eat any of it raw nor boiled in water, but only roasted with fire, the head with the feet and the inner parts.
verses.12:10: You shall not leave any of it until morning, and you shall not break a bone of it; and what remains of it until morning you shall burn with fire.
verses.12:11: And in this way you shall eat it: your waists girded, and your sandals on your feet, and your staffs in your hands; and you shall eat it with haste. It is a Passover to the Lord.
verses.12:12: And I will go through the land of Egypt on this night, and I will strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from man to livestock, and against all the gods of the Egyptians I will execute vengeance; I am the Lord.
verses.12:13: And the blood shall be for you as a sign on the houses where you are; and I will see the blood and will shelter you, and there shall not be among you a plague of destruction when I strike in the land of Egypt.
verses.12:14: And this day shall be to you a memorial, and you shall celebrate it as a feast to the Lord throughout all your generations; as a perpetual statute you shall celebrate it.
verses.12:15: Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, and from the first day you shall remove leaven from your houses; everyone who eats leaven, that soul shall be utterly destroyed from Israel, from the first day until the seventh day.
verses.12:16: And the first day shall be called holy, and the seventh day shall be a holy convocation to you; you shall do no servile work on them, except whatever shall be done for every soul, that alone shall be done by you.
verses.12:17: And you shall keep this commandment, for on this day I will bring out your host from the land of Egypt; and you shall observe this day throughout your generations as a perpetual statute.
verses.12:18: Beginning on the fourteenth day of the first month, from evening, you shall eat unleavened bread until the twenty-first day of the month, until evening.
verses.12:19: Seven days no leaven shall be found in your houses; everyone who eats anything leavened, that soul shall be utterly destroyed from the congregation of Israel, both among the proselytes and among the natives of the land.
verses.12:20: You shall not eat anything leavened, but in every dwelling place of yours you shall eat unleavened bread.'"
verses.12:21: Then Moses called all the council of elders of the sons of Israel and said to them, "Go and take for yourselves a sheep according to your kindred, and you shall sacrifice the Passover.
verses.12:22: And you shall take a bunch of hyssop, and having dipped it into the blood that is beside the door, you shall touch the lintel and both of the doorposts with some of the blood that is beside the door; and none of you shall go out of the door of his house until morning.
verses.12:23: And the Lord will pass by to strike the Egyptians, and He will see the blood on the lintel and on both of the doorposts; and the Lord will pass by the door, and He will not allow the destroyer to enter into your houses to strike.
verses.12:24: And you shall keep this word as a statute for yourself and for your sons forever.
verses.12:25: And when you enter into the land which the Lord gives you, just as He spoke, you shall keep this service.
verses.12:26: And it shall be, when your sons say to you, 'What is this service?'
verses.12:27: that you shall say to them, 'This Passover is a sacrifice to the Lord, as He sheltered the houses of the sons of Israel in Egypt when He struck the Egyptians, but delivered our houses.'" And the people bowed down and worshiped.
verses.12:28: And the sons of Israel went and did just as the Lord commanded Moses; so they did.
verses.12:29: Now it came about at midnight that the Lord struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sat on the throne to the firstborn of the captive woman who was in the pit, and to the firstborn of all livestock.
verses.12:30: And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he and his attendants and all the Egyptians, and there was a great outcry in all the land of Egypt, for there was not a house in which there was not someone dead.
verses.12:31: And Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron in the night and said to them, "Rise up and go out from among my people, both you and the sons of Israel; go and serve the Lord your God, just as you say.
verses.12:32: And taking both your sheep and your cattle, go on your way, and bless me also."
verses.12:33: And the Egyptians were urgently pressing the people to drive them out of the land in haste, for they said, "We are all dying."
verses.12:34: So the people took up the dough before it was leavened, their batches of dough bound up in their garments on their shoulders.
verses.12:35: And the sons of Israel did just as Moses had instructed them, and they asked from the Egyptians articles of silver and gold, and clothing.
verses.12:36: And the Lord gave favor to His people before the Egyptians, and they lent to them; and they plundered the Egyptians.
verses.12:37: Now the sons of Israel set out from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand men on foot, besides the dependents.
verses.12:38: And a great mixed crowd went up with them, and sheep and cattle and very much livestock.
verses.12:39: And they baked the dough which they had brought out of Egypt into unleavened hearth cakes, for it had not been leavened; for the Egyptians drove them out, and they were not able to linger, nor had they prepared provisions for themselves for the journey.
verses.12:40: Now the dwelling of the sons of Israel, which they dwelt in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan, was four hundred thirty-five years.
verses.12:41: And it came about after the four hundred thirty-five years that all the host of the Lord went out from the land of Egypt by night.
verses.12:42: It is a vigil to the Lord for bringing them out from the land of Egypt; that very night is a vigil to the Lord, to be for all the sons of Israel throughout their generations.
verses.12:43: Now the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying, "This is the law of the Passover: no foreigner shall eat of it.
verses.12:44: And as for every household servant or one bought with silver, you shall circumcise him, and then he shall eat of it.
verses.12:45: A temporary resident or a hired worker shall not eat of it.
verses.12:46: In one house it shall be eaten, and you shall not carry any of the flesh outside from the house, and you shall not break a bone of it.
verses.12:47: All the congregation of the sons of Israel shall observe it.
verses.12:48: And if any proselyte comes to you to observe the Passover to the Lord, you shall circumcise every male belonging to him; and then he shall come near to observe it, and he shall be just like the native of the land. No uncircumcised person shall eat of it.
verses.12:49: There shall be one law for the native-born and for the proselyte who has come among you."
verses.12:50: And the sons of Israel did just as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron concerning them; so they did.
verses.12:51: And it came about on that day that the Lord brought the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt with their host.
verses.13:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.13:2: "Consecrate to Me every firstborn, first-offspring, opening every womb among the sons of Israel, from man to livestock; it is Mine."
verses.13:3: And Moses said to the people, "Remember this day on which you went out from the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery; for with a mighty hand the Lord brought you out from here, and leaven shall not be eaten.
verses.13:4: For on this day you are going out, in the month of the new produce.
verses.13:5: And it will be, whenever the Lord your God brings you into the land of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Hivites, and the Girgashites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Jebusites, which He swore to your fathers to give to you, a land flowing with milk and honey, then you shall perform this service in this month.
verses.13:6: Six days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day is a feast of the Lord.
verses.13:7: Unleavened bread you shall eat for seven days; nothing leavened shall be seen with you, nor shall leaven be with you within all your borders.
verses.13:8: And you shall report to your son on that day, saying, 'Because of this the Lord God acted for me, when I was going out of Egypt.'
verses.13:9: And it will be to you a sign upon your hand and a memorial before your eyes, so that the law of the Lord may be in your mouth; for with a mighty hand the Lord God brought you out of Egypt.
verses.13:10: And you shall keep this law from days to days.
verses.13:11: And it will be, when the Lord your God brings you into the land of the Canaanites, in the way He swore to your fathers, and gives it to you,
verses.13:12: then you shall set apart everything opening a womb, the males, to the Lord; everything opening a womb from the herds or among your livestock, as many as you may have, the males you shall consecrate to the Lord.
verses.13:13: Everything opening the womb of a donkey you shall exchange for a sheep; and if you do not exchange it, you shall redeem it. Every firstborn of man among your sons you shall redeem.
verses.13:14: And if your son asks you after these things, saying, 'What is this?' then you shall say to him, 'With a mighty hand the Lord brought us out from the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery;
verses.13:15: and when Pharaoh hardened himself against sending us out, He killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of men to the firstborn of livestock. Because of this I sacrifice every firstborn to the Lord, everything opening a womb, the males, and every firstborn of my sons I will redeem.'
verses.13:16: And it will be for a sign upon your hand, and something immovable before your eyes; for with a mighty hand the Lord brought you out of Egypt."
verses.13:17: Now when Pharaoh sent the people out, God did not lead them by the way of the land of the Philistines, because it was near; for God said, "The people might have regret upon seeing war, and turn back to Egypt."
verses.13:18: And God led the people around by the way into the wilderness, to the Red Sea; and in the fifth generation the sons of Israel went up from the land of Egypt.
verses.13:19: And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him; for with an oath he had made the sons of Israel swear, saying, "The Lord will surely visit you, and you shall carry up my bones from here with you."
verses.13:20: And having departed from Succoth, the sons of Israel encamped at Etham beside the wilderness.
verses.13:21: And God was leading them, by day in a pillar of cloud to show them the way, and by night in a pillar of fire.
verses.13:22: And the pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night did not fail before all the people.
verses.14:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.14:2: "Speak to the sons of Israel, and having turned back, let them encamp opposite the farmstead, between Migdol and the sea, directly facing Baal-zephon; in front of them you shall encamp by the sea;
verses.14:3: and Pharaoh will say to his people, 'These sons of Israel are wandering around in the land; for the wilderness has shut them in.'
verses.14:4: And I will harden the heart of Pharaoh, and he will pursue after them; and I will be glorified in Pharaoh and in all his army, and all the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord." And they did so.
verses.14:5: And it was reported to the king of the Egyptians that the people had fled; and the heart of Pharaoh and the heart of his servants turned against the people, and they said, "What is this we have done, sending out the sons of Israel so that they do not serve us?"
verses.14:6: So Pharaoh yoked his chariots, and led away all his people with him,
verses.14:7: and having taken six hundred chosen chariots and all the cavalry of the Egyptians, and officers over all of them.
verses.14:8: And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt and of his servants, and he pursued after the sons of Israel; now the sons of Israel were going out with a high hand.
verses.14:9: And the Egyptians pursued after them and found them encamped beside the sea; and all the cavalry and the chariots of Pharaoh and the horsemen and his army were opposite the farmstead, directly facing Baal-zephon.
verses.14:10: And Pharaoh was drawing near; and having looked up with their eyes, the sons of Israel saw, and the Egyptians had encamped behind them, and they were greatly afraid. And the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord,
verses.14:11: and they said to Moses, "Because there were no graves in the land of Egypt, have you brought us out to put us to death in the wilderness? What is this you have done to us, having brought us out of Egypt?
verses.14:12: Was not this the word that we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, 'Leave us alone so that we may serve the Egyptians'? For it is better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in this wilderness."
verses.14:13: And Moses said to the people, "Take courage! Stand firm and see the salvation from God, which He will accomplish for us today; for in the way you have seen the Egyptians today, you will never see them again forever.
verses.14:14: The Lord will fight for you, and you shall keep silent."
verses.14:15: And the Lord said to Moses, "Why do you cry out to Me? Speak to the sons of Israel, and let them break camp;
verses.14:16: and you, lift up your staff, and stretch out your hand over the sea and split it, and let the sons of Israel enter into the midst of the sea on the dry ground.
verses.14:17: And look, I will harden the heart of Pharaoh and of all the Egyptians, and they will go in after them; and I will be glorified in Pharaoh and in all his army, and in his chariots and in his horses.
verses.14:18: And all the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord, when I am glorified in Pharaoh and in his chariots and his horses."
verses.14:19: And the angel of God, who was going ahead of the camp of the sons of Israel, moved and went to the rear; and the pillar of cloud also moved from before them and stood behind them.
verses.14:20: And it entered between the Egyptians and the camp of Israel, and stood; and there came darkness and gloom, and the night passed, and they did not come together with one another all night.
verses.14:21: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and the Lord drove back the sea with a violent south wind all night, and made the sea dry, and the water was divided.
verses.14:22: And the sons of Israel entered into the midst of the sea on the dry ground, and the water was a wall for them on the right and a wall on the left.
verses.14:23: And the Egyptians pursued, and went in after them, even every horse of Pharaoh and the chariots and the riders, into the midst of the sea.
verses.14:24: And it came about in the morning watch that the Lord looked upon the camp of the Egyptians in a pillar of fire and cloud, and threw the camp of the Egyptians into confusion,
verses.14:25: and He bound the axles of their chariots and led them with force. And the Egyptians said, "Let us flee from the face of Israel, for the Lord is fighting for them against the Egyptians."
verses.14:26: And the Lord said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand over the sea, and let the water return and cover over the Egyptians, both upon the chariots and the riders."
verses.14:27: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and toward daybreak the water returned to its place; and the Egyptians fled under the water, and the Lord shook off the Egyptians in the midst of the sea.
verses.14:28: And turning back, the water covered the chariots and the riders and all the force of Pharaoh, those who had entered after them into the sea; and not even one of them was left.
verses.14:29: But the sons of Israel walked through dry land in the midst of the sea, and the water was a wall for them on the right and a wall on the left.
verses.14:30: And the Lord rescued Israel on that day from the hand of the Egyptians; and Israel saw the Egyptians dead along the shore of the sea.
verses.14:31: And Israel saw the great hand, what the Lord did to the Egyptians; and the people feared the Lord, and they believed in God and in Moses His servant.
verses.15:1: Then Moses and the sons of Israel sang this song to God, and spoke, saying, "Let us sing to the Lord, for He has been gloriously glorified; horse and rider He hurled into the sea.
verses.15:2: A helper and protector He became to me for salvation; this is my God, and I will glorify Him, the God of my father, and I will exalt Him.
verses.15:3: The Lord is one who crushes wars; the Lord is His name.
verses.15:4: Pharaoh's chariots and his army He hurled into the sea, chosen riders, officers; they were swallowed up in the Red Sea.
verses.15:5: With the deep sea He covered them; they sank down into the depth like a stone.
verses.15:6: Your right hand, Lord, has been glorified in strength; Your right hand, Lord, shattered enemies.
verses.15:7: And by the abundance of Your glory You crushed the adversaries; You sent forth Your wrath, and it devoured them like stubble.
verses.15:8: And through the breath of Your anger the water parted; the waters congealed like a wall, the waves congealed in the midst of the sea.
verses.15:9: The enemy said, 'Pursuing, I will overtake; I will divide spoils, I will fill my soul, I will kill with my sword, my hand will rule.'
verses.15:10: You sent forth Your breath, the sea covered them; they sank like lead in violent water.
verses.15:11: Who is like You among the gods, Lord? Who is like You? Glorified among the holy ones, marvelous in glories, performing wonders.
verses.15:12: You stretched out Your right hand; the earth swallowed them.
verses.15:13: You guided by Your righteousness this people of Yours whom You redeemed; You encouraged them by Your strength to Your holy lodging place.
verses.15:14: Nations heard and became angry; birth pains seized those inhabiting Philistia.
verses.15:15: Then the leaders of Edom hastened; and the rulers of the Moabites, trembling seized them; all those inhabiting Canaan melted away.
verses.15:16: May trembling and fear fall upon them; by the greatness of Your arm let them be turned to stone, until Your people pass by, Lord, until this people of Yours whom You acquired pass by.
verses.15:17: Bring them in and plant them on the mountain of Your inheritance, in Your prepared dwelling place which You fashioned, Lord, a sanctuary, Lord, which Your hands prepared.
verses.15:18: The Lord reigns forever and ever and beyond."
verses.15:19: For Pharaoh's horse went with chariots and riders into the sea, and the Lord brought the water of the sea upon them; but the sons of Israel walked through dry ground in the midst of the sea.
verses.15:20: And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took the tambourine in her hand, and all the women went out after her with tambourines and dances.
verses.15:21: And Miriam led them in song, saying, "Let us sing to the Lord, for He has been gloriously glorified; horse and rider He hurled into the sea."
verses.15:22: Then Moses led the sons of Israel away from the Red Sea, and brought them into the wilderness of Shur; and they traveled three days in the wilderness and did not find water to drink.
verses.15:23: And they came to Marah, and they were not able to drink from Marah, for it was bitter; therefore he named the name of that place Bitterness.
verses.15:24: And the people were grumbling against Moses, saying, "What will we drink?"
verses.15:25: And Moses cried out to the Lord; and the Lord showed him a piece of wood, and he threw it into the water, and the water was made sweet. There He set for him ordinances and judgments, and there He tested him,
verses.15:26: and said, "If you carefully listen to the voice of the Lord your God, and do the things pleasing before Him, and give ear to His commandments, and keep all His ordinances, no disease which I brought upon the Egyptians will I bring upon you; for I am the Lord your God who heals you."
verses.15:27: And they came to Elim, and there were twelve springs of water there and seventy trunks of palm trees; and they encamped there beside the waters.
verses.16:1: And they departed from Elim, and the entire congregation of the sons of Israel came to the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai. And on the fifteenth day of the second month after they had gone out from the land of Egypt,
verses.16:2: the entire congregation of the sons of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron.
verses.16:3: And the sons of Israel said to them, "If only we had died, struck down by the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the pots of meat and ate bread to fullness, because you brought us out into this wilderness to kill this entire congregation with famine."
verses.16:4: And the Lord said to Moses, "Look, I am raining bread for you from heaven, and the people will go out and gather the day's portion day by day, so that I may test them, whether they will walk in My law or not.
verses.16:5: And it will be on the sixth day that they will prepare whatever they bring in, and it will be double whatever they gather day by day."
verses.16:6: And Moses and Aaron said to the entire congregation of the sons of Israel, "At evening you will know that the Lord brought you out from the land of Egypt,
verses.16:7: and in the morning you will see the glory of the Lord, when He hears your grumbling against God; and what are we, that you grumble against us?"
verses.16:8: And Moses said, "When the Lord gives you meat in the evening to eat and bread in the morning to fullness, because the Lord has heard your grumbling which you grumble against us—and what are we? For your grumbling is not against us, but against God."
verses.16:9: And Moses said to Aaron, "Say to the entire congregation of the sons of Israel, 'Approach before God, for He has heard your grumbling.'"
verses.16:10: And as Aaron was speaking to the entire congregation of the sons of Israel, they turned toward the wilderness, and the glory of the Lord appeared in a cloud.
verses.16:11: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.16:12: "I have heard the grumbling of the sons of Israel; speak to them, saying, 'Toward evening you will eat meat, and in the morning you will be filled with bread; and you will know that I am the Lord your God.'"
verses.16:13: And evening came, and quail came up and covered the camp; in the morning it happened, as the dew settled around the camp,
verses.16:14: look, on the surface of the wilderness was something fine like coriander, white like frost on the ground.
verses.16:15: And when the sons of Israel saw it, they said to one another, "What is this?" For they did not know what it was. And Moses said to them, "This is the bread which the Lord has given you to eat.
verses.16:16: This is the word which the Lord commanded: 'Gather from it, each one for those belonging to him; an omer per head, according to the number of your souls, each one with your tentmates, gather.'"
verses.16:17: And the sons of Israel did so, and they gathered, one much and another less.
verses.16:18: And when they measured with the omer, the one with much had no excess, and the one with less had no lack; each gathered for those with him who belonged to him.
verses.16:19: And Moses said to them, "Let no one leave any of it until the morning."
verses.16:20: And they did not listen to Moses, but some left part of it until the morning; and it swarmed with worms and stank; and Moses became embittered against them.
verses.16:21: And they gathered it in the morning; and when the sun grew warm, it melted.
verses.16:22: And it happened on the sixth day that they gathered double the necessary amount, two omers for each one; and all the rulers of the congregation came in and reported to Moses.
verses.16:23: And the Lord said to them, "Is this not the word which the Lord spoke? Tomorrow is a Sabbath, a holy rest to the Lord; whatever you bake, bake, and whatever you boil, boil; and all that is left over, leave it in storage until the morning."
verses.16:24: And they left some of it until the morning, just as Moses commanded them; and it did not stink, nor did a worm appear in them.
verses.16:25: And Moses said, "Eat today, for today is a Sabbath to the Lord; it will not be found in the plain.
verses.16:26: Six days you will gather, but on the seventh day is a Sabbath, because there will be none on it."
verses.16:27: And it happened on the seventh day that some of the people went out to gather, and they found none.
verses.16:28: And the Lord said to Moses, "How long are you unwilling to listen to My commandments and My law?
verses.16:29: See, for the Lord has given you this day; therefore He Himself gave you bread for two days on the sixth day. Each of you will remain in your houses; let no one go out from his place on the seventh day."
verses.16:30: And the people kept the Sabbath on the seventh day.
verses.16:31: And the sons of Israel named its name manna; and it was like coriander seed, white, and its taste was like a cake in honey.
verses.16:32: And Moses said, "This is the word which the Lord commanded: 'Fill the omer with the manna for storage for your generations, so that they may see the bread which you ate in the wilderness when the Lord brought you out from the land of Egypt.'"
verses.16:33: And Moses said to Aaron, "Take one golden jar and put into it a full omer of manna, and you will set it aside before God for safekeeping for your generations."
verses.16:34: Just as the Lord commanded Moses, Aaron set it aside before God for safekeeping.
verses.16:35: And the sons of Israel ate the manna forty years, until they came to the inhabited land. They ate the manna until they arrived at a region of Phoenicia.
verses.16:36: Now the omer was a tenth of the three measures.
verses.17:1: And all the congregation of the sons of Israel departed from the wilderness of Sin according to their encampments by the word of the Lord, and they encamped in Rephidim; and there was no water for the people to drink.
verses.17:2: And the people were reviling Moses, saying, "Give us water so that we may drink." And Moses said to them, "Why do you revile me, and why do you test the Lord?"
verses.17:3: And the people thirsted there for water, and the people grumbled there against Moses, saying, "Why is this that you brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and the livestock with thirst?"
verses.17:4: And Moses cried out to the Lord, saying, "What shall I do with this people? A little longer and they will stone me to death."
verses.17:5: And the Lord said to Moses, "Go ahead of this people, and take with yourself some of the elders of the people; and take in your hand the staff with which you struck the river, and you shall go.
verses.17:6: Here I stand there before you upon the rock in Horeb; and you shall strike the rock, and water shall come out from it, and My people shall drink." And Moses did so before the sons of Israel.
verses.17:7: And he named the name of that place Testing and Reviling, because of the reviling of the sons of Israel and because of testing the Lord, saying, "Is the Lord among us or not?"
verses.17:8: And Amalek came and fought against Israel in Rephidim.
verses.17:9: And Moses said to Joshua, "Choose for yourself able men, and go out and engage in battle against Amalek tomorrow; and look, I stand on the top of the hill, with the staff of God in my hand."
verses.17:10: And Joshua did just as Moses had told him, and he went out and engaged in battle against Amalek; and Moses and Aaron and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
verses.17:11: And it happened that whenever Moses lifted up his hands, Israel prevailed; but whenever he lowered his hands, Amalek prevailed.
verses.17:12: Now the hands of Moses were heavy; and taking a stone they placed it under him, and he sat on it; and Aaron and Hur supported his hands, one on this side and one on that side; and the hands of Moses remained supported until the setting of the sun.
verses.17:13: And Joshua routed Amalek and all his people with the slaughter of the sword.
verses.17:14: And the Lord said to Moses, "Write this down as a memorial in a book, and put it into the ears of Joshua, that I will utterly blot out the memorial of Amalek from under heaven."
verses.17:15: And Moses built an altar to the Lord, and he named its name "The Lord is my refuge,"
verses.17:16: for with a hidden hand the Lord wages war against Amalek from generations to generations.
verses.18:1: Now Jethro, the priest of Midian, the father-in-law of Moses, heard of all that the Lord had done for Israel His own people, for the Lord had brought Israel out of Egypt.
verses.18:2: And Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, took Zipporah, the wife of Moses, after her dismissal,
verses.18:3: and her two sons; the name of one of them was Gershom, saying, "I was a sojourner in a foreign land";
verses.18:4: and the name of the second was Eliezer, saying, "For the God of my father is my helper, and He delivered me from the hand of Pharaoh."
verses.18:5: And Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, and the sons and the wife came out to Moses into the wilderness, where he was encamped at the mountain of God.
verses.18:6: And it was reported to Moses, saying, "Look, your father-in-law Jethro is coming to you, and your wife and your two sons with him."
verses.18:7: And Moses went out to meet his father-in-law, and bowed down to him and kissed him, and they greeted one another; and he brought him into the tent.
verses.18:8: And Moses recounted to his father-in-law all that the Lord had done to Pharaoh and to all the Egyptians for the sake of Israel, and all the hardship that had come upon them on the way, and that the Lord had delivered them from the hand of Pharaoh and from the hand of the Egyptians.
verses.18:9: And Jethro was amazed at all the good things which the Lord had done for them, that He had delivered them from the hand of the Egyptians and from the hand of Pharaoh.
verses.18:10: And Jethro said, "Blessed be the Lord, because He delivered them from the hand of the Egyptians and from the hand of Pharaoh.
verses.18:11: Now I know that the Lord is great above all the gods, because of this, that they attacked them."
verses.18:12: And Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, took whole burnt offerings and sacrifices to God; and Aaron and all the elders of Israel came to eat bread together with the father-in-law of Moses before God.
verses.18:13: And it happened after the next day that Moses sat down to judge the people; and all the people stood beside Moses from morning until evening.
verses.18:14: And when Jethro saw all that he was doing for the people, he said, "What is this that you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone, while all the people stand beside you from morning until evening?"
verses.18:15: And Moses said to his father-in-law, "Because the people come to me to seek a judgment from God.
verses.18:16: For whenever a dispute arises among them and they come to me, I judge each one, and I instruct them in the ordinances of God and His law."
verses.18:17: And the father-in-law of Moses said to him, "You are not doing this matter rightly;
verses.18:18: you will surely waste away with unbearable ruin, both you and all the people who are with you; this matter is heavy for you, you will not be able to do it alone.
verses.18:19: Now therefore listen to me, and I will advise you, and God will be with you. Be for the people in the things pertaining to God, and you shall bring their matters up to God;
verses.18:20: and you shall solemnly testify to them the ordinances of God and His law, and you shall make known to them the ways in which they shall walk and the works which they shall do.
verses.18:21: And look out for yourself from all the people able men, God-fearing, righteous men, hating arrogance, and you shall appoint over them rulers of thousands and rulers of hundreds and rulers of fifties and rulers of tens,
verses.18:22: and they shall judge the people at every hour; and the weighty matter they shall bring up to you, but the minor judgments they shall judge themselves, and they will relieve you and assist you.
verses.18:23: If you do this matter, God will strengthen you and you will be able to endure, and all this people will come to its own place in peace."
verses.18:24: And Moses listened to the voice of his father-in-law, and did all that he had said to him.
verses.18:25: And Moses chose able men from all Israel, and made them over them rulers of thousands and rulers of hundreds and rulers of fifties and rulers of tens,
verses.18:26: and they judged the people at every hour; and every weighty matter they brought up to Moses, but every light matter they judged themselves.
verses.18:27: And Moses sent off his father-in-law, and he departed to his own land.
