verses.35:27: And the rulers brought the emerald stones and the stones for setting for the ephod and the oracle,
verses.35:28: and the compounds and the oil of anointing and the compounding of the incense.
verses.35:29: And every man and woman whose mind moved them to go in to do all the works that the Lord had commanded to be done through Moses—the sons of Israel brought a contribution to the Lord.
verses.35:30: And Moses said to the sons of Israel, "Look, God has called by name Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah,
verses.35:31: and He has filled him with a spirit of wisdom and understanding and knowledge of all things,
verses.35:32: to design according to all the works of master craftsmanship, to work the gold and the silver and the bronze,
verses.35:33: and to carve stone, and to fashion the wood, and to work in every work of wisdom;
verses.35:34: and indeed He has put it in his mind to instruct—both to him and to Eliab the son of Ahisamach from the tribe of Dan;
verses.35:35: He has filled them with wisdom and understanding of mind, to understand how to do all the works of the sanctuary, and to weave the woven and embroidered works with scarlet and fine linen, to do every work of master craftsmanship in embroidery."
verses.36:1: And Bezalel and Eliab and everyone wise in mind, to whom wisdom and knowledge were given in them to understand how to do all the works according to the holy duties, worked according to all that the Lord commanded.
verses.36:2: And Moses called Bezalel and Eliab and all those who had the wisdom, to whom God gave knowledge in the heart, and all those willingly desiring to come forward to the works so as to complete them.
verses.36:3: And they received from Moses all the contributions that the sons of Israel brought for all the works of the sanctuary, to do them; and they were still receiving the things offered from those bringing them in the morning.
verses.36:4: And all the wise ones who were doing the works of the sanctuary came, each one according to his own work which they themselves were doing.
verses.36:5: And he said to Moses, "The people are bringing an abundance for the works that the Lord commanded to do."
verses.36:6: And Moses gave an order, and he proclaimed in the camp, saying, "Let man and woman no longer work for the firstfruits of the sanctuary." And the people were restrained from offering any more.
verses.36:7: And the works were sufficient for them to make the construction, and they left some over in addition.
verses.36:8: And every wise person among those doing the work made the robes of the sanctuary, which are for Aaron the priest, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
verses.36:9: And he made the ephod of gold, and blue, and purple, and spun scarlet, and twisted fine linen.
verses.36:10: And the plates of gold were cut as hairs, so as to weave together with the blue, and the purple, and the thoroughly spun scarlet, and with the twisted fine linen; they made it a woven work,
verses.36:11: shoulder-pieces joining together from both sides, a woven work, intertwined with one another by itself.
verses.36:12: Out of it they made it, of gold, and blue, and purple, and thoroughly spun scarlet, and twisted fine linen, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
verses.36:13: And they made both the emerald stones fastened with clasps, and bordered around, and engraved with the engraving of a signet after the names of the sons of Israel;
verses.36:14: and he placed them upon the shoulders of the ephod, stones of memorial of the sons of Israel, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
verses.36:15: And they made an oracle, a woven work with embroidery, according to the work of the ephod, of gold, and blue, and purple, and thoroughly spun scarlet, and twisted fine linen;
verses.36:16: they made the oracle square and doubled, a span its length and a span its width, doubled.
verses.36:17: And a four-rowed weaving set with stones was woven into it, a row of stones: sardius, and topaz, and emerald, the first row;
verses.36:18: and the second row: carbuncle, and sapphire, and jasper;
verses.36:19: and the third row: ligure, and agate, and amethyst.
verses.36:20: And the fourth row: chrysolite, and beryl, and onyx, encircled with gold and bound together with gold.
verses.36:21: And the stones were twelve after the names of the sons of Israel, inscribed as signets after their names, each one after its own name, for the twelve tribes.
verses.36:22: And they made upon the oracle intertwined fringes, a work of braiding, of pure gold.
verses.36:23: And they made two small gold shields and two gold rings. And they placed the two gold rings upon both ends of the oracle;
verses.36:24: and they placed the braids of gold upon the rings on both sides of the oracle, and into them the two braids,
verses.36:25: and they placed them upon the two small shields; and they placed them upon the shoulders of the ephod opposite on the front.
verses.36:26: And they made two gold rings, and they placed them upon the two corners on the edge of the oracle and upon the edge of the back of the ephod on the inside.
verses.36:27: And they made two gold rings, and they placed them upon both shoulders of the ephod.
verses.36:28: And he bound the oracle tightly from the rings that were on it to the rings of the ephod, held together with the blue, intertwined into the weaving of the ephod, so that the oracle would not become loose from the ephod, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
verses.36:29: And they made the under-robe beneath the ephod, a woven work, wholly blue;
verses.36:30: and the opening of the under-robe in the middle was woven through and intertwined, having a border around the opening so as not to come apart.
verses.36:31: And they made upon the hem of the under-robe underneath small pomegranates as of a blossoming pomegranate, of blue, and purple, and spun scarlet, and twisted fine linen.
verses.36:32: And they made gold bells, and they placed the bells upon the hem of the under-robe all around between the small pomegranates;
verses.36:33: a gold bell and a small pomegranate upon the hem of the under-robe all around, for ministering, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
verses.36:34: And they made tunics of fine linen, a woven work, for Aaron and for his sons,
verses.36:35: and the headdresses of fine linen, and the turban of fine linen, and the undergarments of twisted fine linen,
verses.36:36: and their sashes of fine linen, and blue, and purple, and spun scarlet, the work of an embroiderer, in the manner that the Lord commanded Moses.
verses.36:37: And they made the gold plate, a dedication of the sanctuary, of pure gold; and he wrote upon it letters engraved as of a signet, "Holiness to the Lord";
verses.36:38: and they placed it upon the blue band, so as to rest upon the turban above, in the manner that the Lord commanded Moses.
verses.37:1: And they made ten curtains for the tabernacle;
verses.37:2: twenty-eight cubits was the length of the one curtain; it was the same for all of them; and four cubits was the width of the one curtain.
verses.37:3: And he made the veil of blue, and purple, and spun scarlet, and twisted fine linen, the work of a weaver, cherubim;
verses.37:4: and they placed it upon four incorruptible pillars overlaid with gold; and their capitals were gold, and their four bases were silver.
verses.37:5: And they made the veil of the door of the tabernacle of testimony of blue, and purple, and spun scarlet, and twisted fine linen, a woven work of the cherubim,
verses.37:6: and their five pillars and the rings; and they overlaid their capitals with gold, and the five bases were bronze.
verses.37:7: And they made the courtyard: the parts toward the southwest, hangings of the courtyard of twisted fine linen, a hundred by a hundred;
verses.37:8: and their pillars were twenty, and their bases were twenty.
verses.37:9: And the side toward the north was a hundred by a hundred, and the side toward the south was a hundred by a hundred; and their pillars were twenty, and their bases were twenty.
verses.37:10: And on the side toward the sea, curtains of fifty cubits; their pillars were ten, and their bases were ten.
verses.37:11: And the side toward the east was fifty cubits, the part at the back;
verses.37:12: and their pillars were three, and their bases were three.
verses.37:13: And on the second back, on this side and on that side by the gate of the courtyard, curtains of a hundred and fifty cubits; their pillars were three, and their bases were three.
verses.37:14: All the curtains of the tabernacle were of twisted fine linen;
verses.37:15: and the bases of their pillars were bronze, and their hooks were silver, and their capitals were overlaid with silver, and the pillars were overlaid with silver, all the pillars of the courtyard.
verses.37:16: And the veil of the gate of the courtyard was the work of an embroiderer, of blue, and purple, and spun scarlet, and twisted fine linen, twenty cubits in length, and the height and the width were five cubits, matching the hangings of the courtyard;
verses.37:17: and their pillars were four, and their four bases were bronze, and their hooks were silver, and their capitals were overlaid with silver.
verses.37:18: And they themselves were overlaid with silver, and all the pegs of the courtyard all around were bronze.
verses.37:19: And this is the arrangement of the tabernacle of testimony, just as was commanded to Moses, that the ministry belong to the Levites through Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest.
verses.37:20: And Bezalel the son of Uri, from the tribe of Judah, did just as the Lord commanded Moses,
verses.37:21: and Eliab the son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, who designed as master craftsman the woven works and the needlework and the embroidered works, to weave with the scarlet and the fine linen.
verses.38:2: and he overlaid it with pure gold inside and outside.
verses.38:3: And he cast for it four gold rings, two on the one side and two on the second side,
verses.38:4: wide for the carrying poles so as to carry it with them.
verses.38:5: And he made the mercy seat above the ark out of gold,
verses.38:6: and the two cherubim of gold:
verses.38:7: one cherub on the end of the mercy seat and one cherub on the second end of the mercy seat,
verses.38:8: overshadowing the mercy seat with their wings.
verses.38:9: And he made the table that is set forth from pure gold,
verses.38:10: and he cast for it four rings, two on the one side and two on the second side, wide so as to carry with the carrying poles in them.
verses.38:11: And he made the carrying poles of the ark and of the table, and he overlaid them with gold.
verses.38:12: And he made the utensils of the table, both the dishes and the incense cups and the ladles and the libation bowls with which he will pour drink offerings, of gold.
verses.38:13: And he made the lampstand that gives light of gold,
verses.38:14: solid in its shaft, and the branches from both of its sides;
verses.38:15: from its branches the buds projecting, three from this side and three from that side, equal to one another;
verses.38:16: and their lamp-cups that are on the ends, shaped like almonds, out of them; and the sockets out of them, so that the lamps might be on them, and the seventh socket from the end of the lamp-cup at the top above, solid, wholly of gold;
verses.38:17: and seven gold lamps on it, and its gold tongs, and their gold oil-ladles.
verses.38:18: This man overlaid the pillars with silver, and he cast gold rings for each pillar, and he gilded the bars with gold, and he overlaid the pillars of the curtain with gold, and he made the hooks of gold.
verses.38:19: This man also made the rings of the tent of gold, and the rings of the courtyard and rings for stretching out the covering above of bronze.
verses.38:20: This man cast the silver capitals of the tent, and the bronze capitals of the door of the tent, and the gate of the courtyard; and he made silver hooks for the pillars on the pillars; this man overlaid them with silver.
verses.38:21: This man also made the pegs of the courtyard of bronze.
verses.38:22: This man made the bronze altar out of the bronze firepans that belonged to the men who rebelled with the congregation of Korah.
verses.38:23: This man made all the utensils of the altar, both its firepan and the base and the bowls and the fleshhooks, of bronze.
verses.38:24: This man made for the altar an attachment, a work of network beneath the firepan under it, up to its middle; and he put on it four bronze rings at the four sides of the attachment of the altar, wide for the bars so as to carry the altar with them.
verses.38:25: This man made the holy anointing oil and the compound of incense, the pure work of a perfumer.
verses.38:26: This man made the washbasin of bronze and its base of bronze out of the mirrors of the women who fasted, who fasted beside the doors of the tent of testimony on the day he pitched it;
verses.38:27: and he made the washbasin so that Moses and Aaron and his sons might wash their hands and feet from it when they entered the tent of testimony; or whenever they approached the altar to minister, they would wash from it, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
verses.39:1: All the gold that was worked for the works, throughout all the workmanship of the holy things, came from the gold of the firstfruits: twenty-nine talents and seven hundred twenty shekels, according to the holy shekel.
verses.39:2: And the offering of silver from the numbered men of the congregation was one hundred talents and one thousand seven hundred seventy-five shekels; one drachma per head, half a shekel, according to the holy shekel.
verses.39:3: Everyone passing through the numbering, from twenty years old and upward, amounted to six hundred thousand and three thousand five hundred fifty.
verses.39:4: And the one hundred talents of silver went into the casting of the one hundred capitals of the tent and into the one hundred capitals of the curtain,
verses.39:5: one hundred capitals for the one hundred talents, a talent per capital.
verses.39:6: And the one thousand seven hundred seventy-five shekels they made into the hooks for the pillars, and he overlaid their capitals with gold and adorned them.
verses.39:7: And the bronze of the offering was seventy talents and one thousand five hundred shekels.
verses.39:8: And out of them he made the bases of the door of the tent of testimony,
verses.39:9: and the bases of the gate all around, and the bases of the gate of the courtyard, and the pegs of the tent, and the pegs of the courtyard all around,
verses.39:10: and the bronze attachment of the altar, and all the utensils of the altar, and all the implements of the tent of testimony.
verses.39:11: And the sons of Israel did just as the Lord commanded Moses; so they did.
verses.39:12: Now the remaining gold of the offering they made into utensils for ministering with them before the Lord;
verses.39:13: and the blue and purple and scarlet that were left over they made into ministering garments for Aaron, so as to minister in them in the sanctuary.
verses.39:14: And they brought the garments to Moses, and the tent and its utensils and the bases and its bars and the pillars,
verses.39:15: and you shall enclose the tent, and you shall sanctify all that belongs to it all around. And you shall anoint the altar of burnt offerings and all its utensils,
verses.39:16: and the altar and all its utensils, and the anointing oil and the compounded incense, and the pure lampstand
verses.39:17: and its lamps, the lamps for burning, and the oil for the light,
verses.39:18: and the table of presentation and all its utensils and the loaves that are set forth,
verses.39:19: and the garments of the sanctuary that belong to Aaron, and the garments of his sons for the priesthood,
verses.39:20: and the hangings of the courtyard and the pillars, and the curtain of the door of the tent and of the gate of the courtyard,
verses.39:22: What the Lord commanded Moses, so the sons of Israel made all the equipment.
verses.39:23: And Moses saw all the works, and they had done them in the manner the Lord commanded Moses; so they did them. And Moses blessed them.
verses.40:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.40:2: "On the first day of the first month, at the new moon, you shall set up the tent of testimony,
verses.40:3: and you shall screen the ark of testimony with the veil.
verses.40:4: And you shall bring in the table and set out its presentation, and you shall bring in the lampstand and set its lamps on it.
verses.40:5: And you shall place the golden altar for burning incense before the ark, and you shall place a veil covering over the door of the tent of testimony.
verses.40:6: And you shall place the altar of burnt offerings beside the doors of the tent of testimony.
verses.40:8: And you shall enclose the tent, and you shall sanctify all that belongs to it all around. And you shall anoint the altar of burnt offerings and all its utensils,
verses.40:9: and you shall take the anointing oil and anoint the tent and all that is in it, and you shall sanctify it and all its utensils, and it shall be holy.
verses.40:10: And you shall sanctify the altar, and it shall be holy of holies.
verses.40:12: And you shall bring Aaron and his sons forward to the doors of the tent of testimony, and you shall wash them with water.
verses.40:13: And you shall clothe Aaron with the holy robes, and you shall anoint him and sanctify him to serve as priest to Me.
verses.40:14: And you shall bring his sons forward and clothe them with tunics,
verses.40:15: and you shall anoint them just as you anointed their father, and they shall serve as priests to Me; and it shall be that they have an anointing of priesthood forever, throughout their generations."
verses.40:16: And Moses did all that the Lord commanded him; so he did.
verses.40:17: And it came about in the first month, in the second year of their going out from Egypt, at the new moon, that the tent was set up.
verses.40:18: And Moses set up the tent, and placed the capitals, and inserted the bars, and set up the pillars.
verses.40:19: And he spread out the curtains over the tent, and placed the covering of the tent over it above, as the Lord ordered Moses.
verses.40:20: And taking the testimonies, he put them into the ark, and placed the poles under the ark,
verses.40:21: and he brought the ark into the tent and placed the covering of the veil, and screened the ark of testimony, just as the Lord ordered Moses.
verses.40:22: And he placed the table in the tent of testimony, on the north side of the tent of testimony, outside the veil of the tent,
verses.40:23: and he set out on it loaves of the presentation before the Lord, just as the Lord ordered Moses.
verses.40:24: And he placed the lampstand in the tent of testimony, on the south side of the tent,
verses.40:25: and he set its lamps on it before the Lord, just as the Lord ordered Moses.
verses.40:26: And he placed the golden altar in the tent of testimony, opposite the veil,
verses.40:27: and he offered on it the compounded incense, just as the Lord ordered Moses.
verses.40:29: And he placed the altar of burnt offerings beside the doors of the tent,
verses.40:33: and he set up the court all around the tent and the altar. And Moses finished all the works.
verses.40:34: And the cloud covered the tent of testimony, and the tent was filled with the glory of the Lord.
verses.40:35: And Moses was not able to enter into the tent of testimony, because the cloud was overshadowing it, and the tent was filled with the glory of the Lord.
verses.40:36: Now whenever the cloud went up from the tent, the sons of Israel would break camp with their baggage;
verses.40:37: but if the cloud did not go up, they would not break camp until the day on which the cloud went up.
verses.40:38: For a cloud was upon the tent by day, and fire was upon it by night, before all Israel, in all their marches.

notes.1:5: LXX counts seventy-five persons (matching 4QExod-a and Acts 7:14) rather than the seventy of the Masoretic Hebrew text, and places the notice about Joseph first.
notes.1:7: LXX uses chydaioi egenonto ("teemed," literally "became abundant in crowds") and concludes with an active clause, "and the land multiplied them," where the Hebrew reads "the land was filled with them."
notes.1:11: LXX renders "fortified cities" (instead of "store cities") and adds a third city, "On, which is Heliopolis," not present in the Masoretic Hebrew text.
notes.1:21: LXX has a third-person plural verb ("they made houses for themselves"), whereas the Masoretic Hebrew has God as the singular subject ("He made houses for them").
notes.2:2: LXX uses plural verbs here and in v. 3 ("seeing... they sheltered him... they could"), attributing Moses' concealment to both parents (echoed in Heb 11:23), whereas the Hebrew uses singular verbs for the mother.
notes.2:16: LXX explicitly names the priest of Midian "Jethro" twice in this verse (absent from the Masoretic Hebrew here), while calling him "Reuel" in v. 18.
notes.2:25: LXX reads a passive verb, "and He was made known to them," reflecting a different reading of the Hebrew verb where the Masoretic text reads "and God knew."
notes.3:4: LXX renders the Hebrew response "Here I am" idiomatically as "What is it?" (Ti estin;), and uses "the Lord" (Kyrios) in both clauses where the Hebrew has YHWH followed by Elohim.
notes.3:14: LXX translates the Hebrew divine self-disclosure ontologically with the present participle ho on, "the One who is" (or "the Existing One").
notes.3:17: LXX reads third-person "and He said" (continuing Moses' report to the elders) rather than first-person "and I said"; as in v. 8, LXX lists seven nations by including the Girgashites.
notes.3:19: LXX reads "except by a mighty hand" (ean me meta cheiros krataias), whereas the Masoretic Hebrew reads "and not [even] by a mighty hand."
notes.4:6: The Greek text reads only "like snow" (ὡσεὶ χιών), without the word "leprous" found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.4:16: Literally "the things pertaining to God" (τὰ πρὸς τὸν θεόν), a Septuagint phrasing that expresses Moses' mediatorial role rather than the Hebrew "as God."
notes.4:18: The closing sentence ("And after those many days, the king of Egypt died") appears here in the Septuagint to introduce v. 19, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text omits it at this point.
notes.4:24: The Greek text specifies "an angel of the Lord" (ἄγγελος Κυρίου), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "the Lord" directly.
notes.4:25: The Septuagint reads "she fell down at the feet and said, 'The blood of the circumcision of my child has stopped,'" differing markedly from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "a bridegroom of blood."
notes.5:3: The Greek text reads "has summoned us" (προσκέκληται ἡμᾶς) and "death or slaughter" (θάνατος ἢ φόνος), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "has met with us" and "pestilence or sword."
notes.5:14: The Greek participle λέγοντες ("saying") follows the passive "were flogged" as a Semitic impersonal construction introducing the question asked by Pharaoh's overseers.
notes.5:16: The Septuagint concludes with "Therefore you will wrong your people" (ἀδικήσεις οὖν τὸν λαόν σου), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "but the fault is in your own people."
notes.6:3: The Greek reads "being their God" rather than the Hebrew Masoretic "as God Almighty" (El Shaddai).
notes.6:15: The Greek identifies Shaul's mother as "the Phoenician woman" (Φοινίσσης), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "the Canaanite woman."
notes.6:18: The Greek names Kohath's second son "Issachar" (Ἰσσαχάρ, compared to "Izhar" in 6:21) and gives Kohath's lifespan as 130 years (Hebrew MT: 133).
notes.6:20: The Greek describes Jochebed as the daughter of Amram's paternal uncle (his cousin; Hebrew MT: his father's sister), includes "Miriam their sister," and gives Amram's lifespan as 132 years (Hebrew MT: 137).
notes.6:22: The Greek lists only two sons of Uzziel—omitting Mishael—and reads "Segri" (Σεγρεί) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Sithri."
notes.6:24: The Greek reads "Abiasar" (Ἀβιασάρ) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Abiasaph."
notes.7:9: The Greek uses δράκων ("dragon" or great serpent) here and in 7:10, 7:12, distinct from ὄφις ("snake") in 7:15.
notes.7:13: The Greek reads "just as the Lord had commanded them" (ἐνετείλατο αὐτοῖς), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "just as the Lord had spoken."
notes.7:19: The final clause shifts to an aorist indicative in Greek ("And blood came to be"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text continues the future prediction ("and there shall be blood").
notes.7:26: Verses 7:26–29 follow the Greek and Hebrew verse numbering, corresponding to 8:1–4 in most English versions.
notes.8:1: Chapter 8 verse numbering follows the Septuagint, where 8:1 corresponds to 8:5 in the Hebrew Masoretic Text (the preceding four verses close chapter 7).
notes.8:8: The Greek reads "concerning the appointed time" (horismos) of the frogs, differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("concerning the frogs which He had brought upon Pharaoh").
notes.8:17: "Dog-flies" translates the collective singular Greek kynomyia (literally "dog-fly"), a biting fly, where the Hebrew has "swarms."
notes.8:18: "Goshen" represents the Septuagint spelling Gesem; the verse also concludes with the Septuagint reading "the Lord, the Lord of all the earth."
notes.9:4: "A single thing" renders Greek rheton (literally "a specified thing"), reflecting the Hebrew idiom for "anything."
notes.9:15: Where the Hebrew Masoretic Text is commonly read as a counterfactual past ("I could have stretched out my hand..."), the Septuagint uses future indicatives ("I will strike... I will put to death... you will be wiped out").
notes.9:17: "Lay claim to" translates the Greek middle verb empoieomai with the genitive, meaning to assert ownership over or detain.
notes.9:23: "Thunders" renders Greek phonai (literally "voices" or "sounds"), a Septuagint Hebraism for thunder that recurs in 9:28, 29, 33, and 34.
notes.10:7: The Greek reads "Or do you want to know that Egypt is destroyed?" (without the "not yet" of the Hebrew Masoretic Text) and uses σκῶλον (lit. "thorn, stake, stumbling block") for "snare."
notes.10:10: Greek ἀποσκευή ("baggage, household train, dependents") is the Septuagint's standard rendering for the non-combatant family members and little ones accompanying the men (so also in 10:24).
notes.10:13: The Septuagint reads "a south wind" (ἄνεμον νότον) rather than the Hebrew "east wind," and has no explicit subject "the Lord" before "brought."
notes.10:22: The Greek intensifies the plague with an asyndetic triad—"darkness, gloom, tempest" (σκότος γνόφος θύελλα)—and in 10:23 specifies "from his bed" (κοίτης) where the Hebrew has "from his place."
notes.11:2: The Septuagint adds "secretly" (κρυφῇ) and "clothing" (ἱματισμόν) here, while omitting the parallel clause about each woman asking her neighbor found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.11:3: The Septuagint includes the additional clause "and they lent to them" (καὶ ἔχρησαν αὐτοῖς) and explicitly mentions "in the sight of the Egyptians" alongside Pharaoh and his attendants.
notes.11:7: The verb παραδοξάζει ("acts wondrously / makes a wondrous distinction") is a distinctive Septuagint rendering of the Hebrew verb for setting apart miraculously; the Greek also reads "so that you [singular] may see" (ἴδῃς) rather than "that you [plural] may know."
notes.11:10: The Greek concludes with "he did not listen so as to send away" (οὐκ εἰσήκουσεν ἐξαποστεῖλαι), directly echoing the prediction of Pharaoh's refusal to listen in 11:9.
notes.12:10: The clause "and you shall not break a bone of it" appears here in the Septuagint in addition to 12:46 (absent from the Masoretic Text in v. 10). The Greek spelling of the first two verbs (-εται) is an orthographic variant for the second-person plural future (-ετε), matching the third verb and 12:46.
notes.12:13: Greek σκεπάσω ("I will shelter") renders the Passover verb here and in 12:27, emphasizing protective covering (compare παρελεύσεται, "will pass by," in 12:23).
notes.12:19: Greek γιώραις is a transliteration of the Aramaic term giyora ("proselyte" or "resident alien"), corresponding to προσήλυτος in 12:48–49.
notes.12:22: Greek παρὰ τὴν θύραν ("beside the door," twice) reflects the Septuagint's understanding of the Hebrew term as "threshold" rather than "basin."
notes.12:40: The Septuagint specifies the dwelling as "in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan" and gives the duration as "four hundred thirty-five years" (here and in 12:41, which also adds "by night"), whereas the Masoretic Text reads 430 years in Egypt alone.
notes.13:4: The Septuagint translates the Hebrew month name Abib as "the new things" (ton neon), referring to newly ripening grain and produce.
notes.13:6: The Septuagint reads "six days" before the seventh-day feast, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "seven days."
notes.13:13: The Septuagint reads "you shall redeem it" (lytrose auto), contrasting with the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which reads "you shall break its neck."
notes.13:16: The Septuagint renders the Hebrew term totafot (often translated "frontlets") with asaleuton ("something immovable" or "unshakable").
notes.13:18: The Septuagint reads "in the fifth generation" (pempte genea), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text (chamushim) is usually translated "equipped for battle" or "in battle array."
notes.14:2: The Septuagint renders the Hebrew place name Pi-hahiroth as the common noun "the farmstead" (tes epauleos), here and in 14:9.
notes.14:20: The Septuagint describes darkness and gloom as the night passed, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text mentions the cloud giving light by night to Israel.
notes.14:21: The Septuagint specifies a "south wind" (anemo noto), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text specifies an "east wind."
notes.14:25: The Septuagint reads that the Lord "bound the axles" (synedesen tous axonas) and "led them with force" (egagen autous meta bias), differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "clogged/removed their wheels so that they drove with difficulty."
notes.15:3: The Greek renders the title as "one who crushes wars" (syntribōn polemous), differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "man of war."
notes.15:5: The Greek uses an instrumental dative ("with the deep sea He covered them"), making the Lord rather than the depths the grammatical subject.
notes.15:13: The Greek has "by Your righteousness" (dikaiosynē) and "encouraged" (parekalesas), distinctive Septuagint renderings where the Hebrew has "steadfast love" and "guided."
notes.15:23: The Greek translates the etiology directly into the place name "Bitterness" (Pikria) rather than repeating the transliterated name Marah (Merra).
notes.16:14: The Greek describes the substance as "like coriander, white" (hōsei korion leukon), a Septuagint reading that differs from the Hebrew "flake-like."
notes.16:16: "Omer" represents the Greek transliteration gomor (defined in 16:36 as "a tenth of the three measures"), and "those belonging to him" renders Greek tous kathēkontas.
notes.16:23: The Greek text reads "the Lord said to them" (eipen de Kyrios pros autous) rather than "Moses," followed by the question "Is this not the word which the Lord spoke?"
notes.16:31: "Manna" translates the shorter Greek form man used throughout Exodus 16.
notes.16:35: The Greek reads "a region of Phoenicia" (meros tēs Phoinikēs) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "the border of the land of Canaan."
notes.17:6: The Greek reads "before the sons of Israel," whereas the Hebrew MT reads "in the sight of the elders of Israel."
notes.17:7: Rather than transliterating the Hebrew place names Massah and Meribah, the Septuagint translates them into Greek as Peirasmos ("Testing") and Loidoresis ("Reviling").
notes.17:15: The Septuagint renders the altar's name "The Lord is my refuge" (Kyrios kataphyge mou), differing from the Hebrew MT "Yahweh-Nissi" ("The Lord is my banner").
notes.17:16: The Greek reads "with a hidden hand" (en cheiri kryphaia), whereas the Hebrew MT has the difficult phrase "a hand upon the throne of Yah."
notes.18:9: The Greek uses exeste ("was amazed" or "astonished"), differing from the Hebrew MT "rejoiced."
notes.18:13: The Greek literally says "after the next day" (meta ten epaurion), a formal rendering of the Hebrew idiom for "on the next day."
notes.18:18: The Septuagint adds anypomoneto ("unbearable") to intensify the warning of ruin and exhaustion.
notes.18:21: The Greek reads "hating arrogance" (misountas hyperephanian), whereas the Hebrew MT reads "hating dishonest gain."
notes.19:3: The Septuagint states that God called Moses "from heaven" (ek tou ouranou), whereas the Hebrew MT reads "out of the mountain."
notes.19:13: The Greek instructs that they may ascend when "the sounds and the trumpets and the cloud depart from the mountain," differing significantly from the Hebrew MT "when the ram's horn sounds a long blast."
notes.19:18: The Septuagint reads "all the people were exceedingly amazed," where the Hebrew MT has "the whole mountain trembled violently."
notes.19:22: The Greek apallaxe ap' auton most naturally means "depart from them" (though some render it "remove some of them"), differing from the Hebrew MT "break out against them."
notes.20:12: The Greek includes "so that it may go well with you" and "the good land," aligning with the phrasing of Deuteronomy 5:16.
notes.20:13: In the Septuagint, verses 13–15 order the prohibitions as adultery, theft, and murder, differing from the Masoretic Text order (murder, adultery, theft) and matching citations in Luke 18:20 and Romans 13:9.
notes.20:17: The Greek places "your neighbor's wife" first before "your neighbor's house" and adds "his field," paralleling Deuteronomy 5:21.
notes.20:22: The Greek expands the introduction with "to the house of Jacob and announce to the sons of Israel," echoing Exodus 19:3.
notes.21:6: Greek to kriterion tou theou ("the judgment court of God") renders the Hebrew ha-elohim specifically as a judicial tribunal under God's authority.
notes.21:16: The Septuagint reverses verses 16 and 17 relative to the Masoretic Text, placing speaking evil of parents in verse 16 and kidnapping in verse 17.
notes.21:22: In verses 22–23, the Greek distinguishes between a child not yet fully formed (me exeikonismenon) and one fully formed (exeikonismenon), whereas the Masoretic Text speaks generally of "harm."
notes.21:29: "Before yesterday and before the third day" is a literal Greek rendering of the Hebrew idiom for "previously," and Greek aphanise means "remove" or "do away with" rather than "keep confined."
notes.21:32: The Greek converts the Hebrew weight unit into thirty didrachmas of silver; note also that verse 37 of this chapter corresponds to Exodus 22:1 in the Masoretic Text.
notes.22:2: The Greek reads "he shall die in return" (ἀνταποθανεῖται), assigning capital liability to one who kills a thief in daylight, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text stipulates restitution by the thief.
notes.22:12: The Greek reads "he shall lead him to the prey" (ἄξει αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὴν θήραν), referring to the carcass left by a predator, whereas the Hebrew directs bringing the torn animal as evidence.
notes.22:17: The Greek uses the masculine plural "sorcerers" (φαρμακούς), whereas the Hebrew uses the feminine singular "sorceress."
notes.22:27: The Greek renders Hebrew Elohim as plural "gods" (θεούς), a well-known Septuagint reading that prohibits reviling deities in general alongside rulers.
notes.23:15: The Greek "month of new crops" (μηνὸς τῶν νέων) translates the Hebrew month name Abib (meaning fresh ears of grain).
notes.23:18: The Greek begins with an expansion paralleling Exodus 34:24 ("For when I cast out nations...") and renders "My sacrifice" as "My incense-offering" (θυμιάματός μου).
notes.23:19: The Greek specifies "a lamb" (ἄρνα), whereas the Hebrew specifies a young goat.
notes.23:22: The Greek includes a major expansion drawn from Exodus 19:5-6 ("you shall be to Me a treasured people... These words you shall speak to the sons of Israel") before resuming the conditional promise of protection.
notes.24:5: "Sacrifice of deliverance" translates Greek thysia sōtēriou, the standard Septuagint rendering for the peace/fellowship offering.
notes.24:10: The Greek reads "they saw the place where the God of Israel stood" rather than the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "they saw the God of Israel," avoiding a direct visual depiction of God.
notes.24:11: The Greek reads "of the chosen ones of Israel not even one perished; and they appeared in the place of God," diverging from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("He did not stretch out His hand against the nobles... and they saw God").
notes.24:14: Here ("they said") and in 24:15 ("Moses and Joshua went up"), the Greek explicitly includes Joshua alongside Moses where the Hebrew Masoretic Text speaks only of Moses.
notes.25:5: "Incorruptible wood" renders Greek xyla asēpta (literally "non-rotting wood"), the Septuagint term for acacia wood. Verse 6 of the Hebrew text (listing oil, spices, and incense) is absent in the Greek critical text.
notes.25:17: "Mercy seat" translates Greek hilastērion epithema (literally "propitiatory cover"), shortened to hilastērion in verses 18–22 and rendered consistently as "mercy seat" across Exodus, Leviticus, and Numbers.
notes.25:22: The Greek reads "I will make Myself known to you from there" (gnōsthēsomai), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "I will meet with you there."
notes.25:23: The Greek specifies "a golden table of pure gold," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text describes a table of acacia wood overlaid with gold.
notes.25:35: The Greek specifies a knob under "the two branches" and a knob under "the four branches," and repeats the clause about four nut-shaped cups on the lampstand, differing from the three pairs of two branches in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.26:14: Greek δέρματα ὑακίνθινα ("blue skins") reflects the Septuagint's color-based rendering where the Hebrew Masoretic Text refers to tachash skins.
notes.26:15: Throughout verses 15–29 the Greek uses στύλους ("pillars") and ξύλων ἀσήπτων ("incorruptible wood"), corresponding to "boards" (or "frames") and "acacia wood" in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.26:18: The Greek places the first twenty pillars on the north side (πρὸς βορρᾶν) and the second twenty on the south side (πρὸς νότον, v. 20), reversing the south-then-north order of the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.26:32: Greek κεφαλίδες ("capitals," also in 26:37 and 27:17) denotes decorative pillar tops, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "hooks."
notes.26:34: The Greek instructs covering the ark of the testimony with the veil (κατακαλύψεις τῷ καταπετάσματι), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text instructs placing the mercy seat upon the ark.
notes.27:3: The Greek lists "a rim" (στεφάνην) and "its cover" (καλυπτῆρα) among the altar's bronze fittings, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text lists pots for ashes and shovels.
notes.27:5: Greek αὐτούς ("them," masculine plural) refers back to the four bronze rings of verse 4, placing the rings beneath the grate, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text places the grate beneath the altar's ledge.
notes.27:9: In verses 9–13 the Greek gives the four sides of the courtyard as southwest (λίβα), east (ἀπηλιώτην), the sea/west (θάλασσαν), and south (νότον), differing from the south, north, west, and east sequence of the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.27:14: In verses 14–16 the Greek explicitly specifies τὸ ὕψος ("the height") for the fifteen-cubit and twenty-cubit dimensions flanking and spanning the gate, whereas verse 18 gives the courtyard's height as five cubits.
notes.27:21: Greek τῆς διαθήκης ("the covenant") varies from τοῦ μαρτυρίου ("the testimony") in the same verse and in 26:33–34, reflecting the Septuagint's rendering of the ark's designation here.
notes.28:1: The Greek spells Aaron's second son Abiud (Ἀβιούδ), rendered with standard modern English Abihu throughout Exodus–Numbers.
notes.28:11: In the Septuagint text, verses 11–12 omit the instructions for gold filigree settings found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text, so the preposition 'upon' at the end of verse 11 links directly into verse 12.
notes.28:15: Greek logion literally means 'oracle' (rendered here as 'oracle of judgments'), corresponding to the breastpiece of judgment in the Hebrew text.
notes.28:29: Verses 23–28, which detail the gold rings and cords attaching the breastpiece in the Hebrew text, are absent in the Septuagint; the fastening is summarized at the end of verse 29.
notes.28:30: Greek delosis ('manifestation') and aletheia ('truth') translate the Hebrew Urim and Thummim.
notes.29:5: Greek ἐπωμίδα ("shoulder garment") and λόγιον ("oracle piece") are the Septuagint terms corresponding to the Hebrew ephod and breastpiece; the Greek text here also omits the mention of Aaron's sash found in the Masoretic Text.
notes.29:9: Greek τελειόω ("consecrate," literally "complete" or "perfect") used with "the hands" is the Septuagint technical idiom for priestly ordination, recurring throughout the chapter (vv. 22, 26-35).
notes.29:20: Greek τὸ ἄκρον ("the tip" or "extremity") of the right hand and right foot corresponds to the thumb and big toe; the command to pour the ram's blood against the altar is placed at the end of v. 21 in the Septuagint rather than v. 20.
notes.29:27: Greek ἀφόρισμα ("separated offering") and ἀφαίρεμα ("contribution," literally "that which is taken away") are the Septuagint renderings corresponding to the wave offering and heave offering; similarly, θυμάτων τῶν σωτηρίων in v. 28 is literally "sacrifices of deliverance."
notes.29:45: Greek ἐπικληθήσομαι ("I will be called upon," echoed by ἐπικληθῆναι in v. 46) differs from the Masoretic Text's "I will dwell"; likewise, the Septuagint reads γνωσθήσομαί ("I will be made known") in v. 42 and τάξομαι ("I will give orders") in v. 43.
notes.30:3: The Greek has "its hearth" (escharan) where the Hebrew text reads "its top," referring to the upper burning surface of the incense altar.
notes.30:13: The Greek expresses the sanctuary weights in Hellenistic currency units—didrachmas and obols—rather than Hebrew shekels and gerahs.
notes.30:24: The Greek specifies "iris" (ireos) where the Hebrew text has "cassia."
notes.30:27: The Greek text repeats "the tent of the testimony and all its utensils" here and orders the furnishings in verses 27-28 differently from the Hebrew text.
notes.31:3: The Greek reads "a divine spirit" (pneuma theion), using an adjective rather than the construct phrase "Spirit of God" in the Hebrew text.
notes.31:4: The Greek includes "blue and purple and spun scarlet" among Bezalel's crafts here, in addition to the metals listed in the Hebrew text.
notes.31:6: The Greek gives the name "Eliab" where the Hebrew text reads "Oholiab," and reads "I have given him and Eliab" rather than "I have appointed with him Oholiab."
notes.31:17: The Greek uses two verbs of cessation, "He rested and ceased" (katepausen kai epausato), where the Hebrew text reads "He rested and was refreshed."
notes.32:4: The Greek uses the singular verb "he said" (referring to Aaron) rather than the plural "they said" of the Hebrew text; similarly in 32:6, the verbs for rising early and offering sacrifices are singular.
notes.32:8: The Greek reads "that you commanded them" (addressing Moses) rather than "that I commanded them," and verse 32:9 is absent from the Septuagint text.
notes.32:14: Where the Hebrew text speaks of the Lord relenting from the disaster He planned, the Septuagint states that the Lord "was appeased so as to preserve His people."
notes.32:18: The phrase "those leading off with wine" (ἐξαρχόντων οἴνου) reflects a distinctive Septuagint reading where the Hebrew text refers to the sound of singing.
notes.32:29: "You have filled your hands" preserves the literal Greek idiom for consecration, rendered here as a past indicative statement rather than a command.
notes.33:2: The Greek uses the second-person singular "you will drive out" (addressing Moses) and includes the Girgashite where the Hebrew text lists the Canaanite.
notes.33:11: The Greek spells the name of Joshua's father Naue (Ναυή) throughout the Pentateuch, rendered here with the standard modern English form Nun.
notes.33:13: The Greek reads "reveal Yourself to me; let me see You clearly" (γνωστῶς, literally "knowingly") instead of the Hebrew "show me your ways," and likewise reads "Reveal Yourself to me" in 33:18.
notes.33:19: The Septuagint reads "in My glory" (τῇ δόξῃ μου) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "all my goodness."
notes.34:18: "Month of new things" translates Greek menì ton neon (referring to new crops or produce), the Septuagint rendering of the Hebrew month name Abib.
notes.34:20: "You shall pay a price" reflects the Septuagint reading (timen doseis), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "you shall break its neck."
notes.34:26: "You shall not offer a lamb" reflects the Septuagint wording (ou prosoiseis arna), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "you shall not boil a young goat."
notes.34:29: "Had been glorified" (dedoxastai) translates the Septuagint rendering for the radiance of Moses's face (later echoed in 2 Corinthians 3:7-11), where the Hebrew verb denotes shining or sending out rays.
notes.35:7: "Blue-dyed skins" (dermata hyakinthina) and "rot-resistant wood" (xyla asepta) reflect the Septuagint renderings for the Hebrew tahash skins and acacia wood.
notes.35:9: The Septuagint omits verses 8, 15, 17, and 18 found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text and presents a shorter, rearranged inventory of the tabernacle furnishings in verses 9-19.
notes.35:27: "The oracle" (to logion) is the Septuagint term for the high priest's breastpiece of judgment, emphasizing its function in divine consultation.
notes.35:34: "Eliab" (Eliab) preserves the Septuagint form of the name of the artisan from Dan, corresponding to Oholiab in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.36:1: The Greek text names Bezalel's companion Eliab here and in 36:2 and 37:21, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has Oholiab.
notes.36:8: From 36:8 onward, the Septuagint places the account of making the priestly garments here (corresponding to Hebrew Exodus 39:1-31), before the curtains and courtyard in chapter 37.
notes.36:9: Greek epomis (literally 'shoulder-garment') is the Septuagint term for the priestly ephod, and in the plural (36:11) refers to its shoulder-pieces.
notes.36:15: Greek logion ('oracle') is the Septuagint rendering for the high priest's breastpiece (Hebrew choshen).
notes.36:24: The Greek phrase rendered 'and into them the two braids' (kai eis tas ta dyo emplokia) lacks a noun after the feminine plural article tas, likely due to an early scribal omission (some witnesses supply 'couplings').
notes.37:4: Greek aseptos (literally 'incorruptible' or 'rot-resistant') is the Septuagint's regular rendering for acacia wood.
notes.37:5: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text (36:37), which describes the entrance screen as an embroiderer's work, the Greek text specifies 'a woven work of the cherubim.'
notes.37:7: The Greek text gives the dimensions as 'a hundred by a hundred' here and in 37:9 (where it lists both a north and a south side in addition to the southwest side in 37:7), differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's 'a hundred cubits.'
notes.37:13: The Greek text reads 'a hundred and fifty cubits' for the curtains on the second flank (notos, literally 'back') by the courtyard gate, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'fifteen cubits.'
notes.38:16: Greek lampadia ('lamp-cups') and enthemia ('sockets') describe the almond-shaped cups and lamp-holders on the ends of the lampstand's branches and its central top.
notes.38:20: The Greek uses kephalides ('capitals,' normally pillar-tops) here and in 39:4-5 where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'bases/sockets' in the parallel passages.
notes.38:22: The Septuagint distinctively states that Bezalel made the bronze altar from the firepans of the men who rebelled with Korah's congregation (cf. Numbers 16:36-40), a detail absent from the Hebrew text of Exodus.
notes.38:26: Greek reads 'women who fasted' (nesteusason), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text refers to women who 'served' or 'assembled' at the entrance of the tent.
notes.39:1: The Septuagint gives seven hundred twenty shekels of gold (Hebrew Masoretic Text: seven hundred thirty) and refers to 'the holy shekel.'
notes.39:2: Greek renders the half-shekel weight (Hebrew beka) with the Hellenistic measure 'one drachma.'
notes.39:4: Greek repeats 'one hundred' before both the capitals of the tent and the capitals of the curtain; verse 5 then gives the total of one hundred capitals for one hundred talents.
notes.39:7: The Septuagint records seventy talents and one thousand five hundred shekels of bronze, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads two thousand four hundred shekels.
notes.39:15: The Saints Greek Critical Text adopts at this point wording that its witnesses number as Exodus 40:8 (verse confidence 8%); it is translated here as it stands. Compare 40:8.
notes.40:2: The Septuagint reads "the tent of testimony" (skēnē tou martyriou) and includes "at the new moon" (noumēnia), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "the tabernacle of the tent of meeting" without a separate "new moon" phrase.
notes.40:8: The Septuagint omits v. 7 (the bronze basin, as also vv. 11 and 30-32), reads "enclose the tent" rather than setting up the courtyard, and places the anointing of the altar of burnt offerings here before v. 9.
notes.40:18: The Greek reads "capitals" (kephalidas, the top pieces of pillars) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text refers to bases and frames.
notes.40:35: The Greek verb epeskiazen ("was overshadowing") describes the cloud's presence over the tent; the same verb is echoed in the New Testament for the overshadowing presence of God's cloud and Spirit.
notes.40:36: The Greek reads "with their baggage" (syn tē apartia autōn), a distinct Septuagint rendering where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "throughout all their journeys."
